item.content:encoded:
Finding meaningful employment after graduation remains one of the biggest challenges facing young professionals in Ghana. While thousands of graduates enter the labor market each year equipped with academic qualifications, many employers continue to report difficulties finding candidates with the practical and workplace-ready skills required for immediate employment.

To bridge this gap, the Skills & Innovation Academy, supported by the German Development Cooperation, has introduced an innovative initiative that prepares graduates for employment while helping Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) access qualified, job-ready talent.

The Academy offers free pre-employment training tailored specifically to the real workforce needs of Ghanaian SMEs. The initiative enables businesses to recruit skilled graduates while giving young professionals practical skills that significantly improve their employability.

The program forms part of the Special Initiative “Decent Work for a Just Transition”, operating under the Invest for Jobs brand and funded by Germany’s Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). Implementation is led by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH, with implementation support from MDOZ Company Limited through consulting services.

This initiative represents a practical solution to addressing youth unemployment, strengthening SME competitiveness, and promoting sustainable economic development across Ghana.

About the Skills & Innovation Academy

The Skills & Innovation Academy is designed to close the gap between education and employment by ensuring graduates possess the exact competencies employers are actively seeking.

Unlike conventional training programs that rely on generic curricula, this Academy developed its training after conducting a comprehensive enterprise needs assessment among Ghanaian SMEs.

This assessment identified the skills businesses expect to need over the next one to two years, allowing the Academy to build an industry-driven curriculum that directly reflects employer demand.

As a result, graduates complete training equipped with relevant technical expertise, digital capabilities, workplace competencies, and professional attitudes required to succeed from their very first day on the job.

Why the Program Matters

Small and Medium Enterprises play a crucial role in Ghana’s economy. They generate employment, stimulate innovation, and contribute significantly to economic growth.

However, many SMEs continue to face challenges in recruiting candidates with practical experience and industry-relevant skills.

Research conducted by the Skills & Innovation Academy revealed that, alongside access to finance and markets, access to qualified human resources remains one of the greatest growth opportunities for Ghanaian SMEs.

The Academy therefore focuses on producing graduates who can immediately contribute to business productivity while reducing recruitment and onboarding costs for employers.

What Makes This Program Unique?

The Skills & Innovation Academy distinguishes itself through its employer-centered approach.

Instead of offering generalized training, every aspect of the curriculum has been developed based on the actual hiring needs of Ghanaian businesses.

The training emphasizes practical application, workplace readiness, and future-focused competencies.

Key features include:

  • Employer-informed curriculum
  • Free pre-employment training
  • Industry-specific technical skills
  • Digital skills development
  • Artificial Intelligence (AI) training
  • Workplace safety education
  • Resource-efficient production methods
  • Cleaner production practices
  • Soft skills for professional success
  • Direct connection with hiring SMEs

Training Areas

Participants receive comprehensive training across multiple disciplines designed to improve their employment prospects.

1. Sector-Specific Technical Skills

Graduates gain practical knowledge tailored to industries where SMEs are actively recruiting.

These technical competencies are based on current and anticipated market demand.

2. Digital Skills

Digital literacy has become essential across virtually every industry.

The Academy equips graduates with modern digital competencies that improve workplace productivity and efficiency.

3. Artificial Intelligence (AI)

Recognizing the increasing importance of AI in business operations, the Academy introduces participants to AI tools and technologies relevant to today’s workplace.

Graduates learn how emerging technologies can improve productivity and support business growth.

4. Resource-Efficient and Cleaner Production

Sustainability is becoming increasingly important for businesses worldwide.

Participants are trained in methods that promote efficient resource utilization while reducing environmental impact.

5. Workplace Safety

Understanding workplace health and safety standards helps graduates contribute to safer working environments while meeting employer expectations.

6. Soft Skills Development

Technical knowledge alone is often insufficient for long-term career success.

The Academy therefore emphasizes employability skills including:

  • Professional communication
  • Teamwork
  • Problem-solving
  • Time management
  • Critical thinking
  • Adaptability
  • Professional ethics
  • Leadership potential
  • Customer service
  • Workplace professionalism

These competencies enable graduates to integrate quickly into professional environments.

Benefits for Graduates

Successful participants stand to gain numerous advantages through the Skills & Innovation Academy.

These include:

  • Free professional training
  • Practical workplace preparation
  • Industry-relevant technical skills
  • AI and digital competencies
  • Improved employability
  • Enhanced professional confidence
  • Exposure to employer expectations
  • Opportunity to connect directly with hiring SMEs
  • Increased competitiveness in the labor market
  • Better career prospects

Benefits for SMEs

The Academy also delivers significant value to participating businesses.

Companies benefit from access to graduates who have already received training aligned with their operational needs.

Participating SMEs can expect:

  • Access to trained graduates
  • Reduced recruitment costs
  • Shorter onboarding periods
  • Employees with practical workplace skills
  • Improved workforce productivity
  • Better alignment between recruitment and business growth

The initiative also provides businesses with the opportunity to receive the first selection of trained, job-ready candidates.

SME Vacancy Registration

As part of the initiative, SMEs are invited to submit details of available vacancies through the Skills & Innovation Academy Vacancy Form.

The questionnaire requires approximately 10 minutes to complete.

Businesses use the form to share current or anticipated employment opportunities, which are then matched with trained graduates.

This matching process helps ensure employers receive candidates whose skills correspond to their recruitment needs.

APPLY HERE

Organizations Behind the Initiative

The Skills & Innovation Academy is supported by several respected organizations committed to employment creation and economic development.

These include:

  • German Development Cooperation
  • Invest for Jobs
  • Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
  • Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
  • MDOZ Company Limited

Together, these organizations are helping strengthen Ghana’s workforce while promoting sustainable private-sector growth.

Why This Initiative Is Important

Youth unemployment remains a major development challenge in many countries, including Ghana.

Programs such as the Skills & Innovation Academy contribute to addressing this challenge by creating stronger connections between education, workforce development, and employer demand.

Rather than simply providing academic knowledge, the Academy prepares graduates with practical competencies that employers value most.

At the same time, SMEs gain access to skilled professionals capable of supporting innovation, business expansion, and long-term competitiveness.

This creates a mutually beneficial ecosystem where graduates secure better employment opportunities while businesses strengthen their workforce.

Visit HERE for more information about the Skills & Innovation Academy Ghana.

How to Participate

For Graduates

Eligible graduates interested in improving their employability should participate in the free pre-employment training offered through the Skills & Innovation Academy.

For SMEs

Businesses with available vacancies are encouraged to complete the Skills & Innovation Academy Vacancy Form to access a pool of trained graduates ready for employment.

Application Deadline

No official application deadline has been announced for this opportunity. Interested participants and SMEs are encouraged to apply or register as early as possible.

Conclusion

The Skills & Innovation Academy represents an important investment in Ghana’s future workforce by equipping graduates with practical, employer-driven skills while addressing the recruitment challenges faced by SMEs. Through free, high-quality pre-employment training, participants gain technical expertise, digital and AI competencies, workplace safety knowledge, and essential soft skills that prepare them for immediate employment.

Supported by German Development Cooperation through the Invest for Jobs initiative and implemented by GIZ with MDOZ Company Limited, the Academy serves as a bridge between education and employment, helping graduates launch successful careers while enabling businesses to recruit skilled, job-ready professionals. For graduates seeking to enhance their employability and SMEs searching for qualified talent, this initiative offers a valuable opportunity to contribute to Ghana’s growing economy.

item.content:encoded:
Every educator has a story, experience, or innovative teaching approach that has the potential to inspire thousands—or even millions—of people. However, transforming that knowledge into a memorable public talk requires more than expertise; it requires the ability to communicate ideas clearly, confidently, and effectively.

To help educators unlock this potential, TED-Ed has introduced the TED-Ed Educator Talks Idea Workshop, a completely free virtual professional development experience designed specifically for educators who want to strengthen their storytelling abilities, refine their public speaking skills, and develop ideas worthy of the TED stage.

Led by Logan Smalley, the Founder and Executive Director of TED-Ed and TED’s Head of Education and Learning, this interactive workshop provides participants with practical tools for identifying compelling ideas, crafting impactful messages, and communicating with confidence.

Whether you are an experienced educator, a new teacher, an academic leader, or someone passionate about education, this workshop offers an outstanding opportunity to grow professionally while joining a global community of educators.

What is the TED-Ed Educator Talks Idea Workshop?

The TED-Ed Educator Talks Idea Workshop is a 60-minute live virtual learning experience that serves as the starting point of TED-Ed’s Educator Talks initiative.

The workshop has been designed to help educators:

  • Discover ideas worth sharing.
  • Learn how powerful storytelling creates memorable presentations.
  • Build confidence as public speakers.
  • Connect with fellow educators from around the world.
  • Begin developing a TED-style talk.

Rather than focusing solely on presentation skills, the workshop encourages participants to explore their own experiences in education and identify meaningful lessons that can inspire others.

Participants will leave the session with practical strategies that can be applied in classrooms, conferences, leadership roles, and public speaking opportunities.

Why This Workshop Matters

Educators spend years developing knowledge, solving classroom challenges, mentoring students, and creating innovative learning experiences.

Unfortunately, many valuable educational ideas never reach audiences beyond individual schools or classrooms.

The TED-Ed Educator Talks initiative aims to change that by helping educators transform their expertise into ideas that can influence education globally.

The workshop focuses on helping participants:

  • Clarify their message.
  • Identify meaningful experiences.
  • Organize ideas effectively.
  • Deliver talks with confidence.
  • Inspire audiences through authentic storytelling.

What Participants Will Learn

The workshop combines practical instruction with interactive activities that help educators begin developing their own TED-style presentations.

1. Idea Exploration

Participants will explore what makes ideas memorable and impactful.

This section helps educators:

  • Understand characteristics of compelling ideas.
  • Identify experiences worth sharing.
  • Develop stronger educational narratives.
  • Learn why certain messages resonate with audiences.

2. Interactive Brainstorming

Rather than simply listening to a lecture, attendees actively participate in brainstorming exercises.

Participants will:

  • Reflect on their educational journey.
  • Identify meaningful classroom experiences.
  • Develop repeatable methods for generating presentation ideas.
  • Learn frameworks that can be used repeatedly throughout their careers.

3. Professional Speaker Coaching

One of the workshop’s highlights is learning directly from techniques used by TED’s professional speaker coaches.

Participants will gain practical guidance on:

  • Organizing a presentation.
  • Structuring ideas clearly.
  • Engaging audiences.
  • Building confidence.
  • Delivering memorable presentations.
  • Speaking with authenticity.

What Happens After Completing the Workshop?

The Idea Workshop serves as the first step in a larger professional development journey.

After completing the workshop, educators receive access to additional free learning resources designed to continue developing their public speaking skills.

These include:

TED’s Official Public Speaking Course

Participants gain access to TED’s official public speaking course, where they can continue improving their communication abilities through structured learning materials.

Global Professional Learning Community

Workshop graduates become part of an international community of educators committed to sharing ideas, supporting one another, and exchanging best practices.

This provides opportunities for:

  • Professional networking.
  • Peer collaboration.
  • Continuous learning.
  • Idea sharing across different education systems.

Opportunities to Share Ideas

Participants may also receive opportunities to:

  • Share their ideas with TEDx organizers.
  • Explore speaking opportunities.
  • Start a new TEDx event.
  • Expand the reach of their educational ideas.

Workshop Presenter

The session is led by Logan Smalley, TED’s Head of Education and Learning and the Founding Executive Director of TED-Ed.

Logan brings extensive experience in education, storytelling, and creative communication.

His professional background includes:

  • Founder and Executive Director of TED-Ed.
  • Head of Education and Learning at TED.
  • Director of the award-winning documentary Darius Goes West.
  • Founder of Call Me Ishmael, a literary initiative recognized by the National Book Foundation’s Innovations in Reading Prize.
  • Former high school special education teacher in Athens, Georgia.

His unique combination of classroom teaching experience and global education leadership makes him exceptionally qualified to guide educators through the process of developing powerful public talks.

Benefits of Participating

Educators who attend the workshop will benefit from:

  • Free professional development.
  • Improved storytelling skills.
  • Enhanced public speaking confidence.
  • Practical frameworks for developing impactful ideas.
  • Guidance from TED’s education leadership.
  • Access to TED’s official public speaking resources.
  • Membership in a global educator learning community.
  • Networking opportunities with fellow educators.
  • Potential opportunities to connect with TEDx organizers.
  • Skills applicable to teaching, leadership, conferences, and public presentations.

Why Educators Should Attend

Strong communication is one of the most valuable professional skills educators can possess.

Whether presenting at conferences, leading professional development sessions, teaching students, or advocating for educational change, the ability to communicate ideas effectively creates lasting impact.

The TED-Ed Educator Talks Idea Workshop equips participants with proven communication strategies while encouraging them to discover the unique ideas that only they can share.

Because the workshop is free and accessible online, educators from around the world can participate regardless of location.

Visit HERE for more information about the TED-Ed Educator Talks Idea Workshop 2026.

Registration Information

Interested educators can register for an upcoming virtual session through the official TED-Ed registration platform.

As multiple sessions are available, participants are encouraged to register early for their preferred date and time.

Deadline: No official registration deadline has been announced. Registration remains open while sessions are available.

APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The TED-Ed Educator Talks Idea Workshop is much more than a public speaking class—it is a global professional development opportunity that empowers educators to transform their experiences into inspiring ideas capable of reaching audiences worldwide.

By participating, educators gain access to expert coaching, valuable storytelling frameworks, an international learning community, and continued professional development resources from TED. Whether your goal is to become a more confident speaker, inspire fellow educators, or one day deliver a TED-style talk, this free workshop offers an excellent starting point for that journey.

For more global Training opportunities, visit OFY HERE

item.content:encoded:
UNICEF is offering a self-paced online course on Gender-Responsive Social Protection, designed to help practitioners, development professionals and government partners understand how gender shapes access to opportunity, security, services and well-being throughout a person’s life.

The course introduces the principles and practical application of Gender-Responsive Social Protection, commonly abbreviated as GRSP. It examines how social protection policies and programmes can be designed, delivered, monitored and improved so that they respond to gender-related risks, prevent exclusion and promote dignity, equality and empowerment.

Through interactive exercises, decision-based scenarios, videos, case studies and reflection activities, learners will explore how gender-responsive approaches can improve social protection systems for women, girls and other groups facing intersecting forms of disadvantage.

The activity is delivered online in English and takes approximately two hours to complete. It is open for self-enrollment, and no application deadline is stated.

About the UNICEF Gender-Responsive Social Protection Course

Gender-Responsive Social Protection is an approach that recognizes that women, men, girls, boys and gender-diverse individuals may experience poverty, vulnerability and access to public services differently.

Gender can affect:

  • Who performs unpaid care work
  • Who has access to identification documents
  • Who controls household income
  • Who is able to travel safely to collect payments
  • Who receives information about available programmes
  • Who is formally registered for benefits
  • Who faces discrimination or exclusion
  • Who can use grievance and complaints systems
  • Who is most exposed to economic, environmental or social shocks

A social protection programme may appear neutral while still producing unequal outcomes. For example, a payment system may technically be open to everyone but remain inaccessible to women who lack bank accounts, identification documents, mobile phones, transport or control over household finances.

The course helps learners identify these barriers and consider how programmes can be adjusted to promote fairer and more effective outcomes.

Although the activity is categorized as an advanced e-course, the description presents it as a foundational introduction to Gender-Responsive Social Protection. It therefore provides core concepts while also introducing practical frameworks and tools that can be applied in programme design, delivery, monitoring and advocacy.

The Story-Based Learning Approach

The course follows the story of Mia, an adolescent girl living in a flood-prone coastal town.

Her daily experiences illustrate how gender roles, safety concerns, time pressures and access to documentation can influence whether someone receives social protection support.

As learners progress through the course, they are encouraged to consider questions such as:

  • What barriers make it difficult for Mia to access support?
  • How do household and community expectations affect her choices?
  • Does she have the documents required for registration?
  • Can she safely reach registration or payment locations?
  • Does she have access to information about available services?
  • Are programme staff aware of the gender-related risks she faces?
  • How could the system be redesigned to serve her more effectively?

Mia’s experience provides a practical thread connecting the course modules. It shows that removing barriers for adolescent girls and other excluded groups can improve programme accessibility and effectiveness for the wider population.

Why Gender Matters in Social Protection

Social protection systems are intended to reduce poverty, manage risks and support people during periods of vulnerability. These systems may include cash transfers, social insurance, public employment programmes, food assistance, child benefits, pensions and other forms of support.

However, people do not experience vulnerability in identical ways.

Gender-related inequalities may influence:

  • Employment opportunities
  • Income security
  • Ownership of assets
  • Access to education
  • Exposure to violence
  • Unpaid care responsibilities
  • Mobility
  • Digital access
  • Financial inclusion
  • Participation in decision-making
  • Access to public institutions

These inequalities can become more severe during crises such as floods, conflict, displacement, economic shocks or public-health emergencies.

A gender-responsive approach does not simply add women or girls to an existing programme. It examines how the entire system operates and whether its design, implementation and monitoring address gender-based barriers.

Course Learning Objectives

By the end of the UNICEF Gender-Responsive Social Protection course, learners should be able to achieve the following objectives.

1. Understand Core Concepts

Participants will learn to define and distinguish concepts including:

  • Gender equality
  • Gender equity
  • Intersectionality
  • Social protection
  • Gender responsiveness
  • Inclusion
  • Empowerment

Understanding these terms is important because they shape how programmes identify inequalities and develop appropriate responses.

2. Explain Why Gender Matters

Learners will examine how gender affects risks and vulnerabilities at different stages of life.

These stages may include:

  • Childhood
  • Adolescence
  • Working age
  • Parenthood
  • Older age

Participants will consider how expectations, discrimination and unequal access to resources can influence a person’s ability to benefit from social protection.

3. Apply Gender Analysis

The course introduces gender-analysis frameworks and tools that can be used to assess whether a social protection programme is responsive to the needs of different groups.

Gender analysis may examine:

  • Who has access to resources
  • Who participates in decision-making
  • Who performs paid and unpaid work
  • Who controls income or benefits
  • Who faces safety risks
  • Who is excluded from registration or payments
  • How gender interacts with disability, age, migration status, poverty or location

4. Design Gender-Responsive Interventions

Learners will be introduced to a structured, step-by-step approach for designing or adapting social protection interventions.

This may include:

  1. Identifying gender-related risks and barriers
  2. Understanding the affected population
  3. Reviewing the existing programme design
  4. Selecting practical adjustments
  5. Consulting affected communities
  6. Integrating safeguards
  7. Developing indicators
  8. Monitoring results and unintended consequences

5. Improve Delivery Systems

A well-designed policy can still exclude people if its delivery systems are inaccessible or unsafe.

The course examines key delivery stages, including:

  • Outreach and communication
  • Identification and eligibility assessment
  • Registration
  • Enrollment
  • Payments
  • Referral services
  • Complaints and grievance mechanisms

Learners will consider how each stage can be improved to promote equity and reduce the risk of exclusion, discrimination or harm.

6. Develop Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Plans

Participants will learn how to develop a basic gender-responsive monitoring, evaluation and learning plan.

This may involve:

  • Selecting measurable indicators
  • Collecting gender-disaggregated data
  • Monitoring programme accessibility
  • Assessing whether benefits reach intended groups
  • Identifying unintended harm
  • Gathering feedback from participants
  • Using findings to improve programme delivery

Gender-responsive monitoring should move beyond counting how many women or girls participate. It should examine whether the programme changes access, safety, decision-making, time use, income security or other relevant outcomes.

7. Advocate for Policy and System-Level Change

The course also helps learners understand how evidence, partnerships and inclusive stakeholder engagement can support broader policy change.

Effective advocacy may involve collaboration among:

  • Government ministries
  • Social protection agencies
  • Civil society organisations
  • Women’s rights organisations
  • Youth groups
  • International organisations
  • Donors
  • Researchers
  • Private-sector partners
  • Communities receiving support

8. Demonstrate and Continue Learning

Participants will complete lesson-level knowledge checks and a final assessment.

They will also be introduced to tools and resources that can support continued application after the course.

Course Structure

The UNICEF Gender-Responsive Social Protection e-course consists of five modules.

Module 1: Understanding Gender and Social Protection

The first module introduces the relationship between gender and social protection.

Learners explore concepts such as equality, equity and intersectionality while examining how gender-related inequalities affect vulnerability and access to support.

Module 2: Designing Gender-Responsive Social Protection

This module focuses on programme design.

Participants learn how to apply gender analysis and use a structured approach to develop or adapt social protection interventions.

Module 3: Delivering Gender-Responsive Social Protection

The third module examines delivery systems.

It considers how outreach, registration, enrollment, payment arrangements and grievance mechanisms can either promote inclusion or reinforce existing inequalities.

Module 4: Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning for GRSP

This module introduces gender-responsive monitoring, evaluation and learning.

Learners examine how indicators, data and participant feedback can be used to assess whether a programme is achieving equitable outcomes.

Module 5: Advocacy for Gender-Responsive Social Protection

The final module focuses on advocacy, collaboration and policy change.

It considers how practitioners can use evidence and stakeholder engagement to strengthen gender responsiveness across social protection systems.

Course Methodology

The course uses a self-paced, learner-centred methodology based on modular microlearning.

Learning activities include:

  • Story-based scenarios
  • Decision-based exercises
  • Interactive videos
  • Practical case studies
  • Reflection activities
  • Knowledge checks
  • Instant feedback
  • A final assessment
  • Tools for practical application

The course is grounded in adult-learning principles and has been designed to support inclusive and accessible learning.

Its practical structure allows participants to connect theoretical concepts with real-world social protection challenges.

Course Duration and Format

The estimated completion time is:

Approximately two hours

The course is:

  • Fully online
  • Self-paced
  • Delivered in English
  • Open for self-enrollment
  • Divided into five modules

Because it is self-paced, learners can progress through the materials according to their schedules.

The listing does not state whether participants must complete all modules in one sitting or whether a certificate is awarded. Learners should confirm certification and completion requirements on the enrollment platform.

Who Is the Course Designed For?

The course has a broad professional audience.

It is suitable for:

UNICEF Personnel

  • Country office staff
  • Regional office staff
  • Headquarters personnel
  • Centres of Excellence personnel
  • Consultants
  • Interns
  • Volunteers
  • Goodwill ambassadors
  • Board members
  • National Committee representatives

Government and Public-Sector Professionals

The course may be particularly relevant to officials working in:

  • Social protection
  • Social welfare
  • Gender equality
  • Labour
  • Finance
  • Education
  • Health
  • Child protection
  • Disaster risk management
  • Humanitarian response
  • Monitoring and evaluation
  • Public policy

Civil Society and Development Partners

Non-UNICEF participants may include:

  • Civil society organisations
  • International NGOs
  • Local NGOs
  • Foundations
  • Donors
  • Researchers
  • Universities
  • Advocacy organisations
  • Private-sector partners
  • Social-policy professionals
  • Gender specialists

The course is especially relevant to people involved in programme design, implementation, delivery, evaluation or policy advocacy.

Areas of Professional Relevance

The e-course may support work in areas including:

  • Gender equality
  • Social protection systems
  • Women’s empowerment
  • Adolescent programming
  • Child protection
  • Migration
  • Social inclusion
  • Economic and social policy
  • Risk-informed programming
  • Climate resilience
  • Advocacy
  • Capacity development
  • Monitoring and evaluation
  • Programme operations

Professionals working in crisis-prone or climate-vulnerable environments may find the content particularly useful because the course illustrates how shocks can interact with existing gender inequalities.

Competency Developed

The course is connected to the competency:

Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness

This competency is relevant because gender-responsive programming requires practitioners to reflect critically on assumptions, power relationships and the potential unintended consequences of programme decisions.

It also requires professionals to consider:

  • Whose voices are included
  • Whose needs are overlooked
  • How data is collected and used
  • Whether interventions create additional risks
  • Whether programmes respect dignity and agency
  • How affected communities participate in decisions

How to Enroll

The course is open to self-enrollment.

Prospective learners should access the course page and select the enrollment option provided on the platform.

Before beginning, participants may need to create or sign in to a learning-platform account.

The listing does not mention an application form, competitive selection process or enrollment fee.

ENROLL HERE

Application Deadline

No application or enrollment deadline is stated.

The course appears to remain available for self-enrollment. However, course availability can change, so interested learners should register while the activity remains open.

Contact Information

Content-related questions are directed to:

  • Shreyasi Jha
  • Jessica Owens
  • Lauren Whitehead

The course is connected to UNICEF’s Global Programme Division, Climate Resilience for Children and Technical Assistance team in Bangkok.

Course and learner-management inquiries are directed to Shreyasi Jha.

Learners should use the contact options provided on the official course platform when requesting technical assistance or clarification.

Conclusion

The UNICEF Gender-Responsive Social Protection e-course provides a practical introduction to designing and delivering social protection systems that respond to gender-related inequalities.

Through the story of an adolescent girl living in a flood-prone community, learners examine how safety, time, documentation, social expectations and access to services influence whether people receive support.

The course moves from foundational concepts to practical programme design, delivery, monitoring and advocacy. Its five-module structure equips participants to identify barriers, assess programme responsiveness and propose improvements that promote equality, dignity and inclusion.

With an estimated duration of approximately two hours, a self-paced format and open enrolment, the course is accessible to UNICEF personnel, government officials, civil society partners and other professionals working in gender equality, social protection and inclusive policy.

item.content:encoded:
The Irish Red Cross Migration Policy Project Internship 2026 offers an excellent opportunity for aspiring humanitarian professionals, public policy students, and migration specialists to gain practical experience with one of the world’s leading humanitarian organizations. Based in Dublin, Ireland, this paid internship provides successful applicants with the opportunity to contribute to migration policy initiatives, advocacy work, and event coordination while supporting the Irish Red Cross Migration Department.

If you are passionate about migration, humanitarian action, public policy, and advocacy, this internship provides valuable exposure to real-world policy development and international humanitarian work. Interns will collaborate with experienced professionals, contribute to strategic migration initiatives, and gain insight into how humanitarian organizations influence policy at both national and international levels.

Applications are currently open, and interested candidates are encouraged to submit their applications before the closing date.

About the Irish Red Cross

The Irish Red Cross (IRC) is part of the global Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, one of the largest humanitarian networks in the world. The Movement consists of 190 National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC).

The organization’s mission is to prevent and alleviate human suffering by strengthening humanitarian action and improving the resilience of vulnerable communities both in Ireland and internationally.

Working with the Irish Red Cross gives interns the opportunity to contribute to meaningful humanitarian initiatives while learning from experienced professionals working on migration and advocacy issues.

Internship Overview

Organization: Irish Red Cross

Internship Title: Migration Policy Project Intern

Location: Dublin, Ireland

Internship Period: September – December 2026

Working Schedule: Two days per week (to be agreed)

Working Hours: 9:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. GMT (Flexible)

Monthly Stipend: €800

Application Deadline: 2 August 2026 (11:00 p.m.)

Interview Date: 6 August 2026

About the Internship

The Migration Policy Project Internship has been designed to support the policy-related activities of the Irish Red Cross Migration Department.

A major focus of the internship will be supporting the organization’s engagement around the European Union Presidency and assisting with the planning and coordination of related events. Throughout the internship, successful applicants will work closely with the Migration Department on projects aligned with departmental priorities and the intern’s own experience, competencies, and interests.

This internship combines policy research, advocacy support, event planning, stakeholder engagement, and administrative coordination, making it an excellent opportunity for individuals interested in humanitarian policy careers.

Internship Responsibilities

The selected intern will support a variety of policy and advocacy activities, including:

  • Assisting with logistical planning and coordination for migration-related events.
  • Supporting the Migration Department’s engagement around the EU Presidency.
  • Monitoring Oireachtas debates related to migration.
  • Tracking Parliamentary Questions concerning migration policy.
  • Assisting in the development of migration advocacy materials.
  • Supporting ongoing migration advocacy initiatives.
  • Conducting policy-related research.
  • Providing administrative support where required.
  • Assisting with communications and stakeholder engagement.
  • Performing additional duties as assigned according to departmental priorities.

Since the Irish Red Cross operates in a dynamic humanitarian environment, responsibilities may evolve throughout the internship based on organizational needs.

Internship Benefits

Successful interns will enjoy numerous professional development opportunities, including:

  • Monthly stipend of €800
  • Hands-on experience within an internationally recognized humanitarian organization
  • Practical exposure to migration policy and humanitarian advocacy
  • Opportunity to work alongside experienced policy professionals
  • Networking opportunities within the global Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement
  • Experience in policy research and advocacy
  • Event planning and coordination experience
  • Flexible working arrangements that accommodate candidates’ availability
  • Responsibility for meaningful project work
  • Enhanced understanding of humanitarian operations and migration issues

Eligibility Criteria

Applicants should demonstrate a strong interest in migration policy and humanitarian work.

Candidates should possess:

  • Demonstrated knowledge of migration policy through undergraduate or postgraduate studies.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong interpersonal and teamwork abilities.
  • Initiative and sound professional judgement.
  • Familiarity with social media and communication strategies.
  • Experience in organizing or managing events.
  • Good administrative and organizational skills.
  • Computer proficiency suitable for policy and administrative work.

Applicants with previous experience in advocacy, policy research, humanitarian work, or public affairs will be well positioned for this opportunity.

Why Apply?

The Irish Red Cross Migration Policy Project Internship provides more than workplace experience—it offers an opportunity to contribute to humanitarian policy that directly impacts vulnerable communities.

Interns will gain practical insight into migration policy development, advocacy campaigns, stakeholder engagement, and humanitarian operations while building skills that are highly valued in international organizations, government institutions, NGOs, and policy think tanks.

This internship is ideal for individuals considering future careers in:

  • Migration Policy
  • Humanitarian Affairs
  • International Development
  • Public Policy
  • Human Rights
  • International Relations
  • Advocacy
  • Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs)

Application Process

Interested applicants should:

  1. Visit the official Irish Red Cross careers page.
  2. Read the complete internship description.
  3. Prepare an updated CV and supporting documents.
  4. Submit the online application before the deadline.
  5. Await interview invitations for shortlisted candidates.

Applicants should ensure that all required information is submitted before the application deadline.

Important Dates

  • Applications Close: 2 August 2026 (11:00 p.m.)
  • Interviews: 6 August 2026
  • Internship Duration: September – December 2026

Apply Here

Apply through the official Irish Red Cross Careers website before 2 August 2026 at 11:00 p.m.

Conclusion

The Irish Red Cross Migration Policy Project Internship 2026 is an outstanding opportunity for students and emerging professionals seeking practical experience in migration policy, humanitarian advocacy, and public affairs. Through meaningful project work, policy research, event coordination, and collaboration with one of the world’s most respected humanitarian organizations, interns will develop valuable professional skills while contributing to initiatives that promote humanitarian impact and resilience. If you are passionate about migration policy and international humanitarian work, this internship offers an excellent pathway to build your career while making a positive contribution to society. Discover more internship opportunities like this on the OFY Webpage .

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the Academic Talent Development Program Fellowship 2026, commonly referred to as the ATDP Fellowship Program 2026. This six-month paid professional development opportunity is designed for ambitious young people who want to gain practical workplace experience, strengthen their professional capabilities, and contribute to meaningful projects across education, business, technology, administration, finance, customer service, and related areas.

Based in Accra, Ghana, the ATDP Fellowship combines structured training, professional mentorship, monthly financial support, and practical work exposure. The program aims to prepare emerging professionals for the modern workplace by helping them develop relevant technical, administrative, interpersonal, and problem-solving skills.

Successful fellows will participate in hands-on learning activities and receive guidance from experienced professionals throughout the six-month program. Fellows may also be given an opportunity to undertake an internship with the Academic Talent Development Program or one of its partner organizations.

Young professionals and early-career individuals who meet the age, location, and digital proficiency requirements are encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline.

About the Academic Talent Development Program Fellowship 2026

The Academic Talent Development Program Fellowship is a six-month paid development program created to support the next generation of talent across education, business, and technology.

The fellowship is intended for passionate, driven, and ambitious individuals who are ready to build practical experience and improve the professional skills needed to succeed in a competitive employment environment.

Rather than focusing only on theoretical instruction, the ATDP Fellowship emphasizes practical exposure. Participants will have an opportunity to learn directly from experienced professionals, work on relevant assignments, understand workplace expectations, and apply their skills in real professional settings.

The program is particularly valuable for young people seeking to bridge the gap between academic knowledge and professional employment. It offers participants an environment in which they can develop confidence, improve their workplace readiness, and gain experience that may strengthen their future employment and career prospects.

Key Information About the ATDP Fellowship Program 2026

The main details of the opportunity are as follows:

  • Program name: Academic Talent Development Program Fellowship 2026
  • Common name: ATDP Fellowship Program 2026
  • Program duration: Six months
  • Program type: Paid professional fellowship
  • Location: Accra, Ghana
  • Eligible age range: 20 to 30 years
  • Application deadline: 30 July 2026
  • Application time: Approximately five minutes
  • Selection process: Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted
  • Financial support: Monthly stipends
  • Completion recognition: Certificate upon successful completion
  • Professional exposure: Possible internship placement with ATDP or one of its partner organizations

Applicants should carefully review all eligibility conditions before submitting the application. They must also be prepared to commit to the full six-month duration of the program.

Objectives of the ATDP Fellowship

The ATDP Fellowship is designed to provide young people with the knowledge, skills, experience, and professional guidance required to improve their career readiness.

Its major objectives include:

  1. Providing practical professional experience

The fellowship gives participants an opportunity to gain hands-on experience rather than relying only on classroom-based learning. Fellows may participate in projects, assignments, administrative activities, research, customer engagement, educational initiatives, or technology-related work, depending on their assigned fellowship area.

This practical exposure can help participants understand how professional organizations operate and how individual roles contribute to wider institutional objectives.

  1. Developing in-demand workplace skills

Modern employers increasingly look for candidates with a combination of technical knowledge and strong workplace competencies. The fellowship is designed to help participants strengthen skills that are relevant across different sectors.

These may include:

  • Communication
  • Teamwork
  • Time management
  • Digital literacy
  • Research
  • Documentation
  • Customer service
  • Problem-solving
  • Professional writing
  • Presentation skills
  • Administrative coordination
  • Project support
  • Workplace ethics
  • Accountability

The exact skills developed will depend on the participant’s assigned area and responsibilities.

  1. Connecting fellows with experienced mentors

Mentorship is one of the main components of the program. Fellows will receive guidance from experienced professionals who can help them better understand workplace expectations, professional conduct, career development, and practical problem-solving.

Mentors may also provide feedback on participants’ work, support their professional growth, and help them identify areas that require improvement.

  1. Preparing young professionals for future employment

The fellowship is intended to improve participants’ preparedness for internships, entry-level jobs, entrepreneurship, further training, or other professional opportunities.

By the end of the program, fellows should have gained a better understanding of professional environments and developed stronger evidence of their capabilities.

  1. Supporting meaningful impact through education and innovation

The program also seeks individuals who are interested in contributing to education, innovation, business development, technology, and talent development.

Participants may be involved in initiatives that support learners, institutions, businesses, educators, professionals, or communities, depending on their fellowship placement.

ATDP Fellowship Areas

Applicants may be considered for different fellowship areas based on their interests, experience, qualifications, and the requirements of the program.

The advertised fellowship areas are explained below.

  1. EdTech and Artificial Intelligence

The EdTech and Artificial Intelligence area is suitable for applicants interested in the use of technology to improve education, learning delivery, content development, institutional management, or educational access.

Participants in this area may gain exposure to subjects such as:

  • Digital learning platforms
  • Educational technology tools
  • Artificial intelligence applications
  • Online learning systems
  • Digital content development
  • Technology-supported teaching
  • Research on emerging technologies
  • Data and information management
  • Innovation in education
  • Technology-based problem-solving

Applicants interested in this area should be comfortable working with digital tools and willing to learn about the growing role of technology and artificial intelligence in education and professional services.

  1. Business Development and Customer Service

The Business Development and Customer Service area is intended for applicants who want to understand how organizations identify opportunities, communicate with customers, develop partnerships, improve services, and support institutional growth.

Fellows in this area may gain experience in:

  • Customer communication
  • Client relationship management
  • Market research
  • Business development support
  • Partnership identification
  • Lead generation
  • Customer feedback
  • Service improvement
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • Proposal and presentation preparation
  • Business documentation
  • Brand and service promotion

Strong communication, professionalism, organization, and interpersonal skills may be particularly valuable for applicants interested in this fellowship area.

  1. Administration and Finance

The Administration and Finance area may be appropriate for applicants interested in organizational operations, office management, documentation, budgeting, recordkeeping, financial administration, or general institutional support.

Participants may be exposed to activities involving:

  • Administrative coordination
  • Document preparation
  • Filing and recordkeeping
  • Meeting support
  • Scheduling
  • Data entry
  • Financial documentation
  • Basic budgeting support
  • Expense tracking
  • Spreadsheet management
  • Report preparation
  • Office communication
  • Compliance with administrative procedures

Applicants interested in this area should demonstrate attention to detail, confidentiality, accuracy, organization, and competence in Microsoft Office or Google Workspace applications.

  1. Global Scholars

The Global Scholars area appears to focus on supporting learners or aspiring scholars seeking access to academic, professional, or international development opportunities.

Depending on the structure of the program, participants in this area may support activities relating to:

  • Academic opportunity research
  • Scholarship information
  • Student guidance
  • Educational advising
  • Application support
  • Global learning opportunities
  • Research and documentation
  • Communication with applicants
  • Educational content development
  • Professional development resources

The specific responsibilities of Global Scholars fellows have not been fully detailed in the available application information. Applicants should therefore provide accurate information about their educational interests, research abilities, communication skills, and experience supporting students or young professionals.

  1. Olympiad Certified Teaching Fellow

The Olympiad Certified Teaching Fellow area is likely intended for applicants interested in teaching, academic coaching, learner development, subject-based competitions, and education support.

Participants selected for this area may be involved in:

  • Supporting learners
  • Assisting with academic preparation
  • Developing educational materials
  • Facilitating lessons or learning sessions
  • Coaching students
  • Supporting Olympiad-related preparation
  • Tracking learner progress
  • Conducting academic research
  • Assisting educational professionals
  • Promoting effective teaching and learning practices

The official advertisement identifies this area as Olympiad Certified Teaching Fellow, but the available application material does not provide detailed subject requirements or specify whether applicants must already hold an Olympiad teaching certification. Applicants interested in this track should answer all application questions truthfully and provide any relevant teaching, tutoring, academic, or competition-related experience.

Benefits of the ATDP Fellowship Program

Selected fellows will receive several professional and developmental benefits during the six-month program.

Six months of structured professional experience

The fellowship provides an extended period of workplace exposure, allowing participants to develop their skills gradually and gain meaningful experience over six months.

This duration may enable fellows to participate in projects from their initial planning stages through implementation, monitoring, and completion.

Paid fellowship with monthly stipends

Fellows will receive monthly stipends during the program.

The exact stipend amount has not been stated in the provided application information. Applicants should not assume a particular amount unless it is formally communicated by the organizers.

Hands-on training

Participants will receive practical training intended to strengthen their ability to perform professional responsibilities.

Hands-on training may involve supervised assignments, workplace tools, digital platforms, research tasks, project support, administrative duties, customer engagement, educational initiatives, or other responsibilities connected to the fellow’s assigned area.

Mentorship from experienced professionals

Selected fellows will have access to professional mentorship. This provides an opportunity to learn from individuals with practical experience in their respective fields.

Mentorship can help fellows:

  • Set professional development goals
  • Improve the quality of their work
  • Address weaknesses
  • Build confidence
  • Develop stronger workplace habits
  • Understand professional standards
  • Make informed career decisions

Certificate upon successful completion

Fellows who successfully complete the program will receive a certificate.

The certificate may serve as formal evidence of participation and completion and can be included in a curriculum vitae, professional portfolio, job application, or online professional profile.

Potential internship opportunity

Participants may have an opportunity to undertake an internship with ATDP or one of its partner organizations.

The wording of the announcement indicates that this is an opportunity rather than a guaranteed placement for every fellow. Internship availability may depend on performance, organizational needs, available placements, and the selection decisions of ATDP or its partner institutions.

Exposure to professional networks

Through interactions with mentors, staff members, partner organizations, and other fellows, participants may expand their professional networks.

These connections can be valuable for learning, collaboration, referrals, professional guidance, and future career opportunities.

Improved employability

The combination of practical experience, mentorship, digital skills, workplace exposure, and certification may help fellows become more competitive when applying for future jobs, internships, training programs, or further development opportunities.

Eligibility Requirements for the ATDP Fellowship 2026

Applicants must meet the following requirements.

Age requirement

Applicants must be between 20 and 30 years old.

The available announcement does not explain whether applicants who are exactly 20 or exactly 30 are eligible, but the standard meaning of the stated age range indicates that both ages are included.

Location requirement

Applicants must live within Accra, Ghana.

This is an important condition because the fellowship is Accra-based. Applicants should apply only if they currently live in Accra or can meet the program’s attendance and location requirements.

The announcement does not state that relocation assistance, accommodation, or transportation support will be provided.

Digital proficiency

Applicants must be proficient in the use of:

  • Microsoft Office Suite; or
  • Google Workspace

Relevant applications may include:

  • Microsoft Word
  • Microsoft Excel
  • Microsoft PowerPoint
  • Microsoft Outlook
  • Google Docs
  • Google Sheets
  • Google Slides
  • Google Drive
  • Gmail
  • Google Meet
  • Google Calendar

Applicants should be prepared to demonstrate their ability to use digital productivity tools for communication, document preparation, recordkeeping, presentations, reporting, scheduling, and collaboration.

Availability for the full program

Applicants must be able to commit to the full six-month duration of the fellowship.

Candidates should consider their academic schedule, employment responsibilities, personal commitments, travel plans, and other obligations before applying.

Interest in professional development

Although not presented as a formal technical requirement, the program is intended for passionate, driven, and ambitious individuals who are willing to learn and contribute.

Applicants should demonstrate genuine motivation and a clear interest in gaining practical experience.

Is a University Degree Required?

The available fellowship announcement does not specify a mandatory university degree, diploma, academic discipline, grade point average, or minimum level of education.

Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that a particular academic qualification is required unless additional instructions appear inside the application form or are communicated by the organizers.

Candidates should accurately provide their educational background, professional training, certifications, and relevant experience when completing the application.

Application Process

Interested applicants should complete the official ATDP Fellowship application form.

The application is expected to take approximately five minutes to complete.

Applicants should follow these steps:

  1. Review the fellowship areas and identify the area most closely connected to their interests and capabilities.
  2. Confirm that they are between 20 and 30 years old.
  3. Confirm that they live within Accra.
  4. Ensure that they can commit to the full six-month program.
  5. Prepare accurate personal, educational, and professional information.
  6. Complete all required questions in the application form.
  7. Upload any documents requested through the form.
  8. Review all responses carefully.
  9. Submit the application before 30 July 2026.
  10. Retain any submission confirmation received after applying.

The Google Form indicates that the applicant’s Google Account name, email address, and profile photo may be recorded when files are uploaded and the form is submitted.

Applicants should therefore make sure they are signed in using an appropriate and accessible email account.

Official Application Link

Applications can be submitted through the official Google Form:

Click HERE to apply.

Applicants may also access the form by scanning the QR code provided on the official fellowship advertisement.

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the ATDP Fellowship Program 2026 is:

30 July 2026

Applicants are strongly advised not to wait until the final day. Submitting early can reduce the risk of internet problems, incomplete uploads, login difficulties, or last-minute errors.

Applications submitted after the deadline may not be considered unless the organizers formally announce an extension.

Selection Process

Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted for the next stage of the selection process.

This means that submitting an application does not automatically guarantee:

  • Shortlisting
  • Selection
  • Participation
  • Internship placement
  • Employment
  • Future engagement with a partner organization

Applicants should provide clear, accurate, and relevant responses that demonstrate their suitability for the program.

The available announcement does not specify:

  • The number of available fellowship positions
  • Whether interviews will be conducted
  • The expected program start date
  • The amount of the monthly stipend
  • Daily or weekly working hours
  • Whether the fellowship is fully on-site, hybrid, or partially remote
  • Whether transportation or accommodation support will be provided
  • Whether all fellows will receive an internship placement

Shortlisted candidates should request clarification on these matters if they are invited to the next stage.

How to Prepare a Strong ATDP Fellowship Application

Applicants can improve the quality of their applications by following the guidance below.

Select the most relevant fellowship area

Choose a fellowship area that genuinely matches your interests, education, skills, or prior experience.

For example:

  • Applicants with technology or digital learning interests may consider EdTech and Artificial Intelligence.
  • Applicants with communication and commercial interests may consider Business Development and Customer Service.
  • Applicants with accounting, recordkeeping, office management, or organizational interests may consider Administration and Finance.
  • Applicants interested in scholarships and academic development may consider Global Scholars.
  • Applicants with teaching, tutoring, coaching, or academic competition experience may consider Olympiad Certified Teaching Fellow.

Demonstrate motivation with specific examples

Avoid generic statements such as “I am passionate” without supporting evidence.

Instead, explain:

  • What you have already done in the relevant area
  • What skills you want to develop
  • Why the fellowship matters to your career
  • How you can contribute to ATDP
  • What impact you hope to make

Highlight relevant digital skills

Since Microsoft Office or Google Workspace proficiency is required, applicants should mention practical experience using these tools.

Examples may include:

  • Preparing reports in Microsoft Word
  • Managing data in Microsoft Excel
  • Creating presentations in PowerPoint
  • Collaborating through Google Docs
  • Organizing information in Google Sheets
  • Managing files through Google Drive
  • Scheduling meetings through Google Calendar

Keep information accurate

Do not exaggerate qualifications, employment experience, certifications, or technical expertise.

Application information may be reviewed or verified during the selection process.

Review the application before submission

Check:

  • Spelling
  • Grammar
  • Contact details
  • Uploaded documents
  • Selected fellowship area
  • Educational information
  • Employment information
  • Availability
  • Motivation responses

A carefully completed application creates a stronger professional impression.

Important Considerations Before Applying

Prospective applicants should consider the following points:

  • The fellowship is based in Accra.
  • Applicants must be between 20 and 30 years old.
  • Participants must commit to six months.
  • The fellowship is paid, but the stipend amount has not been disclosed.
  • Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.
  • An internship opportunity may be available, but it is not described as guaranteed for every participant.
  • Limited fellowship spots are available.
  • The deadline is 30 July 2026.
  • Applicants should use accurate contact information that they check regularly.

Why the ATDP Fellowship May Be Valuable

Many young professionals face difficulty entering the workforce because employers often require practical experience, while early-career applicants may not yet have had an opportunity to gain that experience.

The ATDP Fellowship may help address this challenge by combining workplace exposure, mentorship, skills development, financial support, and certification.

The program may be particularly useful for applicants who:

  • Want to gain their first structured professional experience
  • Need practical exposure after completing academic studies
  • Want to improve their digital and administrative skills
  • Are exploring careers in education, business, technology, finance, or customer service
  • Want mentorship from experienced professionals
  • Need stronger evidence of professional competence
  • Want to build a professional network
  • Are interested in potential internship opportunities

However, applicants should evaluate the opportunity based on their own career goals, availability, location, and preferred fellowship area.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the ATDP Fellowship paid?

Yes. The announcement describes it as a six-month paid fellowship and states that fellows will receive monthly stipends.

What is the stipend amount?

The stipend amount has not been stated in the provided application materials.

How long does the fellowship last?

The fellowship lasts for six months.

Where is the program based?

The program is based in Accra, Ghana.

What is the eligible age range?

Applicants must be between 20 and 30 years old.

Can applicants outside Accra apply?

The eligibility criteria state that applicants should live within Accra. Applicants outside Accra may not meet the stated location requirement unless the organizers provide an exception.

Is the fellowship open to international applicants?

The announcement does not provide a nationality requirement. However, applicants must live within Accra and be available for the fellowship.

Is a degree required?

No specific degree requirement is mentioned in the available announcement.

What computer skills are required?

Applicants must be proficient in Microsoft Office Suite or Google Workspace.

Will every fellow receive an internship?

The announcement states that fellows will have the opportunity to undertake an internship with ATDP or a partner organization. It does not confirm that every participant is guaranteed an internship placement.

Will fellows receive a certificate?

Yes. Fellows will receive a certificate upon successful completion of the program.

How long does the application take?

The application is expected to take approximately five minutes.

Will every applicant receive a response?

No. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted for the next stage.

When is the deadline?

The application deadline is 30 July 2026.

Conclusion

The ATDP Fellowship Program 2026 offers a valuable six-month paid professional development opportunity for young people living in Accra who want to strengthen their practical skills and gain workplace experience.

With fellowship areas covering EdTech and Artificial Intelligence, Business Development and Customer Service, Administration and Finance, Global Scholars, and Olympiad Certified Teaching, the program accommodates applicants with a range of professional interests.

Selected fellows will benefit from hands-on training, mentorship, monthly stipends, certification, and possible internship exposure through ATDP or one of its partner organizations.

Applicants should confirm that they meet the age, location, digital proficiency, and availability requirements before submitting the application. Because only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and limited places are available, candidates should submit complete and carefully reviewed applications as early as possible.

The final deadline for applications is 30 July 2026.

item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) has officially opened the Expression of Interest (EOI) for organizations and individuals interested in hosting sessions during the Children & Youth Resilience Hub at UNCCD COP17. This initiative offers a unique opportunity for accredited participants to contribute to one of the world’s leading environmental conferences by organizing discussions, workshops, presentations, and collaborative events focused on combating desertification, land degradation, drought resilience, climate adaptation, and sustainable development.

The Children & Youth Resilience Hub has been designed to amplify the voices of young leaders and strengthen youth participation in global environmental policymaking. Through innovative sessions, networking events, and collaborative dialogues, the Hub aims to bring together youth organizations, technical experts, policymakers, researchers, government representatives, and development partners committed to building a more resilient future.

If you are already confirmed to attend UNCCD COP17, this is your opportunity to showcase your work, share innovative solutions, and engage with international stakeholders working toward land restoration and climate resilience.

About UNCCD and Youth Engagement

The United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) recognizes young people as key drivers of environmental action and sustainable development. Youth around the world continue to develop innovative approaches that address some of the most pressing environmental challenges, including:

  • Desertification
  • Land degradation
  • Drought resilience
  • Climate adaptation
  • Ecosystem restoration
  • Sustainable land management
  • Community resilience

To strengthen youth participation, UNCCD has introduced several important initiatives, including:

  • UNCCD Youth Caucus
  • Land Heroes Campaign
  • Capacity Building Marketplace
  • Support for the Decent Jobs for Youth Initiative
  • UNCCD Youth Engagement Strategy (YES)

These initiatives ensure that young people actively participate in decision-making processes while contributing innovative ideas and practical solutions to environmental challenges.

What is the Children & Youth Resilience Hub?

The Children & Youth Resilience Hub serves as an inclusive platform during UNCCD COP17 where youth and partners can engage in meaningful dialogue and collaborative action.

The Hub seeks to:

  • Promote meaningful youth engagement.
  • Showcase youth-led innovations.
  • Encourage knowledge sharing.
  • Build partnerships across sectors.
  • Facilitate policy discussions.
  • Strengthen advocacy on land restoration.
  • Promote sustainable development.
  • Advance climate adaptation initiatives.
  • Foster collaboration among global stakeholders.

Rather than being a traditional conference venue, the Hub creates an interactive space where participants can exchange ideas, present successful initiatives, and inspire practical action.

Objectives of the Hub

The Children & Youth Resilience Hub has several important objectives, including:

1. Promote Youth Leadership

The Hub highlights the important role young people play in addressing environmental challenges while creating opportunities for youth leadership at the international level.

2. Share Innovative Solutions

Participants will have the opportunity to showcase projects, research findings, community initiatives, and technological innovations that contribute to land restoration and drought resilience.

3. Encourage Collaboration

The platform encourages partnerships among:

  • Governments
  • NGOs
  • Youth organizations
  • International agencies
  • Researchers
  • Private sector partners
  • Community organizations

4. Strengthen Advocacy

The Hub provides space for young people to influence conversations around:

  • Climate adaptation
  • Land restoration
  • Environmental sustainability
  • Desertification
  • Drought resilience
  • Sustainable development

Who Can Submit a Session Proposal?

The Expression of Interest is only open to applicants who are already confirmed participants of UNCCD COP17.

Potential applicants include:

  • Youth organizations
  • Civil society organizations
  • International organizations
  • NGOs
  • Universities
  • Research institutions
  • Technical experts
  • Government partners
  • Community organizations
  • Development agencies
  • Accredited individuals

Applicants must already possess confirmed accreditation to participate in COP17.

Important Eligibility Requirement

One of the most important conditions of this opportunity is that submission of an Expression of Interest does not provide registration or accreditation for UNCCD COP17.

Applicants must already:

  • Be officially confirmed participants.
  • Hold valid accreditation for COP17.
  • Make their own travel arrangements.
  • Secure accommodation.
  • Obtain any required visas.
  • Cover all participation expenses independently.

The UNCCD Youth Caucus will not provide funding for:

  • Travel
  • Accommodation
  • Visa costs
  • Registration
  • Meals
  • Local transportation
  • Any other participation-related expenses

Applicants should therefore ensure that all logistical arrangements have already been completed before submitting a proposal.

Session Formats Available

Applicants may choose from several engaging session formats depending on the nature of their proposed event.

Available formats include:

  • Presentation
  • Workshop
  • Panel Discussion
  • Interactive Activity
  • Open Dialogue
  • Roundtable Discussion

Each format allows participants to engage audiences differently while contributing to the goals of the Children & Youth Resilience Hub.

Thematic Areas

Applicants should clearly indicate the thematic focus of their proposed session.

Possible themes may include:

  • Desertification
  • Land degradation
  • Drought resilience
  • Climate adaptation
  • Sustainable development
  • Youth leadership
  • Environmental innovation
  • Community resilience
  • Nature-based solutions
  • Land restoration
  • Climate policy
  • Ecosystem conservation

Sessions should demonstrate how they contribute to the overall objectives of COP17 and the Children & Youth Resilience Hub.

Information Required During the Application

Applicants will be required to complete several sections within the Expression of Interest form.

These include:

Organizational Information

  • Organization name
  • Partner information

Contact Details

  • Primary contact person
  • Email address
  • Phone number (preferably WhatsApp)

Alternate Contact

  • Alternate contact person
  • Email
  • Phone number

Online Presence

Applicants should provide:

  • Organization website
  • Social media links

Session Proposal Requirements

Applicants must submit a concise description of their proposed event.

The description should include:

  • Thematic focus
  • Objectives
  • Expected outcomes
  • Contribution to COP17
  • Contribution to the Children & Youth Resilience Hub goals

The proposal should not exceed 350 words.

VIP Participation

Applicants will also be asked whether they intend to invite:

  • Ministers
  • Government officials
  • International leaders
  • Other VIP participants

This information helps organizers coordinate scheduling and logistics where appropriate.

Event Scheduling

Applicants are required to select:

  • One preferred session date and time
  • One alternative session date and time

Multiple scheduling options are available throughout the duration of COP17, providing flexibility for organizers while helping the Hub accommodate a wide range of activities.

Applicants should note that final scheduling decisions remain subject to availability and overall conference programming.

Confirmation Requirement

Before submitting the form, applicants must confirm that they understand:

  • Session times may change.
  • Session formats may be adjusted.
  • Scheduling depends on availability and conference planning requirements.

Why You Should Participate

Hosting a session at the Children & Youth Resilience Hub provides numerous professional and networking benefits.

These include:

  • Present your work to a global audience.
  • Share innovative environmental solutions.
  • Build international partnerships.
  • Connect with policymakers.
  • Collaborate with technical experts.
  • Engage youth leaders from around the world.
  • Increase visibility for your organization.
  • Contribute to international environmental policy discussions.
  • Support global efforts on land restoration and drought resilience.
  • Strengthen youth participation in sustainable development initiatives.

For more information about the UNCCD Youth Caucus, Click HERE.

Financial Considerations

Applicants should carefully note that this opportunity is not a funding program.

Participants are fully responsible for financing:

  • Airfare
  • Accommodation
  • Visa expenses
  • Registration
  • Meals
  • Insurance
  • Local transportation
  • Any additional participation costs

Only applicants who have already secured these arrangements should apply.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should complete the official Expression of Interest form by providing all requested organizational and session information.

Before applying, ensure that:

  1. You are already accredited for UNCCD COP17.
  2. Your proposed session aligns with the objectives of the Children & Youth Resilience Hub.
  3. Your proposal clearly explains its contribution to COP17.
  4. You have selected your preferred session format and scheduling options.
  5. You understand that submitting an application does not guarantee acceptance.

APPLY HERE.

Deadline

No application deadline has been specified in the available announcement. Applicants are encouraged to submit their Expression of Interest as early as possible before the COP17 scheduling process is finalized.

Conclusion

The UNCCD COP17 Children & Youth Resilience Hub offers an outstanding platform for accredited youth leaders, organizations, and environmental stakeholders to contribute meaningfully to one of the world’s most important conferences on land restoration and climate resilience. By organizing presentations, workshops, discussions, or interactive activities, participants can showcase innovative solutions, build global partnerships, and strengthen youth engagement in sustainable development. While the opportunity does not include financial support or conference accreditation, it provides a valuable avenue for qualified COP17 participants to influence international dialogue and collaborate with experts committed to combating desertification, land degradation, and drought.
