item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the 42nd Cycle of the National PhD Programme in Sustainable Development and Climate Change for the 2026–2027 academic year.

Coordinated by the Scuola Universitaria Superiore IUSS Pavia in Italy, this three-year doctoral programme brings together universities, public research institutions, professors, researchers and specialized research groups from across Italy. It is designed to train a new generation of researchers, experts and decision-makers capable of addressing the interconnected challenges of climate change, sustainability, technological transition, economic development, health, environmental protection and social transformation.

A total of 35 funded PhD positions are available under the 2026 call. Each position is linked to a specific research project and host institution, meaning applicants must carefully examine the available research topics before choosing the project or projects that best match their academic background, research experience and professional interests.

The application deadline is:

August 26, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. Central European Summer Time

Applications must be completed exclusively through the official online PICA application platform. A non-refundable application fee of €30 must also be paid before the deadline.

About the National PhD Programme in Sustainable Development and Climate Change

The National PhD Programme in Sustainable Development and Climate Change, commonly referred to as PhD-SDC, is an interdisciplinary doctoral programme established to prepare researchers to respond to some of the most complex environmental and societal challenges facing the world.

Rather than treating climate change as an isolated scientific issue, the programme studies the relationships among:

  • Climate systems and environmental change;
  • Human health and well-being;
  • Biodiversity and ecosystems;
  • Availability of natural resources;
  • Food and water security;
  • Technological development;
  • Energy transition;
  • Migration and human rights;
  • Economic and social development;
  • Territorial vulnerability;
  • Institutions and public policy;
  • Sustainable production and consumption;
  • Quality of life for present and future generations.

The programme seeks to move beyond traditional single-discipline doctoral education. Its structure combines different scientific languages, research methods and academic disciplines so that doctoral candidates can develop solutions that reflect the complex nature of sustainable development and climate change.

Programme Duration and Language

The PhD programme lasts three years and is taught primarily in English.

All multidisciplinary and curriculum-level educational activities, together with most specialized courses, are conducted in English. The final doctoral thesis must also be written in English.

Candidates are expected to possess a good working knowledge of English. However, a formal English-language certificate is not necessarily required when submitting the application. Successful candidates must obtain a recognized B2-level English-language certificate by October 31, 2027, which is the end of the programme’s first academic year.

Number of Funded PhD Positions

The 2026 call provides 35 PhD positions.

The number may be increased before the programme begins where additional funding becomes available.

Each funded position is connected to:

  • A specific research topic;
  • A designated host university or research institution;
  • One of the programme’s three curricula;
  • A research supervisor or reference person;
  • Defined research objectives and expected outputs;
  • In some cases, a mandatory internship or external placement.

Candidates are not applying for a general, unrestricted PhD position. They must indicate interest in specific research topics, and their research proposal must be prepared around the topic selected as their first preference.

Applicants may be considered only for topics for which the selection committee determines that they possess the necessary academic knowledge, skills and research potential.

Three Research Curricula

The 42nd Cycle of the programme is organized into three broad but interconnected research curricula.

  1. CU Alpha – One Health: Earth System and Human Life

This curriculum examines the relationship between the Earth’s systems, ecosystems, biodiversity, climate change, human activity, health and well-being.

Research under this curriculum may address areas such as:

  • Atmospheric and climate modelling;
  • Climate extremes;
  • Environmental and human health;
  • Ecosystem resilience;
  • Biodiversity;
  • Earth observation;
  • Food and water systems;
  • Climate-related health risks;
  • Interactions between environmental conditions and human life;
  • Planetary health and One Health approaches.

The curriculum is particularly relevant to candidates with backgrounds in environmental science, climate science, Earth science, biology, ecology, medicine, health sciences, agriculture, atmospheric science, environmental engineering or related fields.

  1. CU Beta – Human Society: Socio-Economic Impacts, Institutions and Theories

This curriculum examines how climate change and sustainability affect communities, institutions, economies, policies and social systems.

Research may focus on:

  • Climate-related social and economic risks;
  • Environmental policy and governance;
  • Sustainable economic models;
  • Institutional responses to climate change;
  • Social vulnerability;
  • Public decision-making;
  • Climate adaptation and resilience;
  • Sustainable mobility;
  • Disaster risk and recovery;
  • Urban systems;
  • Inequality, justice and migration;
  • Behavioural and policy responses under uncertainty.

It may be suitable for candidates in economics, public policy, sociology, political science, international relations, law, governance, development studies, geography, urban planning, disaster management and other social-science disciplines.

  1. CU Gamma – Technology and Territory: Sustainable Strategies and Solutions for the Transition

This curriculum focuses on technological, engineering, territorial and industrial solutions that can support the transition toward climate-resilient and sustainable societies.

Potential research areas include:

  • Renewable energy;
  • Building decarbonization;
  • Artificial intelligence and sustainability;
  • Remote sensing;
  • Life-cycle assessment;
  • Circular economy;
  • Precision agriculture;
  • Sustainable food systems;
  • Smart and resilient cities;
  • Internet of Things technologies;
  • Water-resource management;
  • Sustainable materials;
  • Offshore energy;
  • Geothermal resources;
  • Sustainable industrial processes;
  • Climate-resilient infrastructure.

The curriculum is particularly relevant to candidates in engineering, computer science, energy systems, environmental technology, architecture, agriculture, industrial ecology, materials science, urban planning and related disciplines.

Examples of Research Topics Available in 2026

The complete 2026 research-topic catalogue includes projects covering environmental science, health, economics, public policy, technology, agriculture, energy, artificial intelligence, infrastructure and territorial development.

Examples listed on the official research-topic platform include:

  • Lunar infrared observations of the Earth for climate and weather research;
  • Climate-smart weed control and microbial biostimulants;
  • Global and regional climate modelling;
  • Remote sensing and hydrological modelling;
  • Life-cycle assessment of biological solutions;
  • Artificial intelligence-driven life-cycle assessment;
  • Sustainable crop protection;
  • Offshore renewable-energy systems;
  • Sustainable nutraceutical systems;
  • Tropical crop management under climate change;
  • Building-sector decarbonization;
  • Geothermal energy, carbon capture and critical raw materials;
  • Artificial intelligence and Internet of Things solutions for climate-resilient environments;
  • Plant adaptation to changing environmental conditions;
  • Functional foods and circular-economy models;
  • Urban water-footprint reduction;
  • Decision-making under deep uncertainty;
  • Social impacts of earthquake-related power outages;
  • Alpine flood resilience;
  • Sustainable transport and mobility.

Applicants must read the description of their preferred project carefully. Each project may specify particular academic skills, methodological competencies, host institutions, supervisors, internship obligations and research expectations.

Participating Universities and Research Institutions

IUSS Pavia serves as the administrative and coordinating institution for the National PhD Programme.

For the 42nd Cycle, the official call identifies the following participating universities and research institutions as operational locations for the programme:

  1. Politecnico di Milano;
  2. Politecnico di Torino;
  3. Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa;
  4. Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna;
  5. University of Bari Aldo Moro;
  6. Free University of Bozen-Bolzano;
  7. Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore;
  8. University of Insubria;
  9. Mediterranean University of Reggio Calabria;
  10. University of Messina;
  11. University of Naples Federico II;
  12. University of Naples L’Orientale;
  13. University of Palermo;
  14. University of Perugia;
  15. University of Pisa;
  16. University of Turin;
  17. University of Trento;
  18. National Research Council of Italy.

The exact host institution assigned to a successful candidate depends on the research topic attached to the awarded position. Although the programme is coordinated nationally by IUSS Pavia, candidates will normally perform their primary research activities at the host institution identified in the relevant research-topic description.

Programme Structure

The academic programme operates through three complementary levels of education.

Horizontal or Multidisciplinary Training

Multidisciplinary activities bring together candidates from different curricula and academic backgrounds.

These events help students understand the broader complexity of climate change and sustainability by exposing them to perspectives beyond their immediate research specialization.

Vertical or Curriculum-Based Training

Curriculum activities provide training in the tools, theories, methodologies and research questions relevant to each of the three principal curricula.

These activities allow students working in related fields to exchange ideas and establish interdisciplinary research connections.

Focused and Disciplinary Training

Specialized courses are delivered by the host universities and research institutions.

These courses are intended to provide the technical, theoretical and methodological knowledge required for each candidate’s individual doctoral project.

The programme website highlights more than 160 hours of training and seminars, international research exposure and access to an extensive network of universities, professors and researchers.

Financial Support and Scholarship Value

Each awarded position carries an annual scholarship of:

€18,645.63 per year

This amount includes the social-security contributions charged to the doctoral candidate. It is exempt from Italian personal income tax known as IRPEF, but it is subject to contributions under the Italian INPS separate social-security scheme.

Two-thirds of the applicable social-security contribution is paid by the administration, while one-third is borne by the doctoral candidate. Therefore, applicants should understand that the published annual value is not the same as the final amount received after applicable deductions.

Scholarship Duration

The scholarship covers the full three-year duration of the programme.

It is initially awarded for the first year and renewed annually, subject to a positive assessment of the candidate’s academic and research progress by the programme’s Academic Board.

Increased Funding for Research Abroad

For an approved period of research outside Italy, the scholarship may be increased by 50%.

The international research period is normally around six months, although the increased scholarship may be authorized for a total period of up to 12 months.

Additional Research Budget

Each PhD candidate also receives an annual research budget equal to at least 20% of the scholarship value.

This separate budget may be used to support authorized research expenses in Italy and abroad, according to the programme’s internal rules. It may help cover activities such as research visits, fieldwork, conferences, specialized training or other project-related expenses.

Insurance

Doctoral candidates are insured against accidents and civil liability for the entire duration of the programme.

Eligibility Requirements

Applications are accepted from qualified candidates without restrictions based on age or nationality.

Candidates must possess at least one of the following qualifications:

  • An Italian Laurea Magistrale;
  • An Italian Laurea Specialistica;
  • A degree awarded under Italy’s previous university system;
  • An equivalent second-level qualification from an Italian higher artistic, musical or performing-arts institution;
  • A foreign qualification comparable in duration and academic content to an Italian master’s degree.

Foreign qualifications are assessed by the selection committee exclusively for admission to the doctoral competition.

Candidates who have not yet completed their qualifying master’s degree may apply conditionally. However, the required qualification must be obtained no later than the programme’s starting date of November 1, 2026.

Is There an Age Limit?

There is no stated minimum or maximum age limit.

The call explicitly welcomes qualified candidates regardless of age. Selection is based on academic qualifications, research potential, the quality of the submitted proposal, the letter of purpose and interview performance.

Is the Programme Open to International Applicants?

Yes. Candidates from both European Union and non-European Union countries may apply.

International applicants must possess a qualification that is academically comparable to an Italian master’s degree. They must provide appropriate degree certificates, transcripts and, where applicable, official translations.

Successful non-EU candidates will also need to complete the required Italian student-visa and residence-permit procedures.

Documents Required for the Application

Applicants must upload all required documents through the official online application portal.

  1. Valid Identification Document

Applicants must submit a clear scan of both sides of a valid photographic identification document.

Where the document is written in a non-Latin alphabet, an authorized translation is required. Documents without the required translation may not be accepted.

  1. Curriculum Vitae

The curriculum vitae must:

  • Be written in English;
  • Contain no more than 2,000 words;
  • Describe the applicant’s education and academic training;
  • Include relevant employment or research experience;
  • List publications, where applicable;
  • Present any additional academic or professional qualifications relevant to the selected project.

Applicants should tailor the CV to the research topic rather than submitting an unfocused general résumé.

  1. Proof of the Qualifying Degree

The degree documentation should include:

  • Name of the awarding university;
  • Type and title of the degree;
  • Academic specialization or major;
  • Graduation date or expected graduation date;
  • Final grade;
  • List of examinations completed;
  • Grades awarded for each examination.

Applicants with degrees from universities in EU or non-EU countries should normally provide the degree certificate, academic transcript or Diploma Supplement where available.

  1. Evidence of Other Academic Qualifications

Candidates may submit supporting records for additional bachelor’s degrees, master’s degrees or other university qualifications.

These documents should provide the same type of information required for the principal qualifying degree.

  1. Documents for Candidates Awaiting Their Master’s Degree

Candidates who have not completed their master’s degree by the application deadline must provide evidence of the examinations completed and the grades received.

They must subsequently obtain the required degree by November 1, 2026.

  1. Research Proposal

The research proposal must:

  • Be written in English;
  • Contain between 1,000 and 2,500 words, excluding the bibliography;
  • Address the research topic selected as the applicant’s first preference;
  • Include an abstract of no more than 250 words;
  • Define the scope of the proposed research;
  • Present clear research questions;
  • Explain the methodology;
  • Identify expected results;
  • Describe the anticipated academic, environmental, technological, social or policy impact.

The research proposal is one of the most heavily weighted components of the selection process.

  1. Letter of Purpose

The letter of purpose must:

  • Be written in English;
  • Contain no more than 500 words;
  • Explain the applicant’s motivation for undertaking the proposed research;
  • Focus primarily on the first-preference research topic;
  • Explain interest in any other topics selected;
  • Connect the applicant’s education, skills and experience to the proposed projects.

Document Language and Translation Requirements

Most application materials must be submitted in English.

Degree certificates, transcripts and similar academic documents may be presented in:

  • Italian;
  • English;
  • French;
  • Spanish.

Documents issued in another language must be accompanied by an official translation into either Italian or English. The translation should be prepared by the degree-awarding university, an authorized organization or an authorized translator.

Failure to provide required documents or translations may result in exclusion from the selection process.

How to Apply

Applicants should complete the following steps:

  1. Open the official PICA application platform for the 42nd Cycle.
  2. Log in using an existing account or select “New Registration.”
  3. Enter the required personal and contact information.
  4. Activate the account through the confirmation email.
  5. Select the relevant curriculum and preferred research topic or topics.
  6. Upload the curriculum vitae.
  7. Upload a valid identification document.
  8. Upload the degree certificate, transcript or evidence of expected graduation.
  9. Upload the research proposal.
  10. Upload the letter of purpose.
  11. Add any other relevant qualifications or supporting records.
  12. Save the application and return to the applicant dashboard.
  13. Use the verification function to check the information entered.
  14. Pay the €30 application fee through the PagoPA system.
  15. Sign and formally submit the application.
  16. Confirm that an application-submission email has been received.

Applicants who do not receive the confirmation email within 24 hours should contact the PICA technical support service. Saving an incomplete application is not the same as formally submitting it. Click HERE to apply.

Selection Process

Selection is based on academic and professional qualifications followed by an online interview.

Candidates can receive a maximum of 100 points.

Stage One: Assessment of Qualifications

The document-assessment stage carries a maximum of 60 points:

  • Curriculum vitae and academic qualifications: up to 20 points;
  • Research proposal and letter of purpose: up to 40 points.

Applicants must obtain at least 35 points to be invited to the interview.

The committee may determine during this stage that an applicant is not academically suitable for one or more selected research topics.

Stage Two: Online Interview

The interview carries a maximum of 40 points.

It will:

  • Be conducted online;
  • Be held in English;
  • Examine the candidate’s scientific and academic background;
  • Discuss the research proposal;
  • Examine the letter of purpose;
  • Assess suitability for the selected research topic;
  • Verify possession of the necessary disciplinary knowledge.

Candidates may use presentation slides and screen-sharing functions during the interview.

A minimum interview score of 25 points is required to remain eligible.

Interviews will be conducted through Microsoft Teams. Candidates must connect with both video and audio and must present valid identification. Failure to attend at the designated time or failure to provide identification will be treated as withdrawal from the competition.

Ranking and Assignment of Positions

Final rankings will be prepared separately for each curriculum.

Candidates will be ranked according to their total scores. In the event of a tie, priority will be given to the younger candidate.

Positions will be offered according to:

  • The final ranking;
  • The research topics for which the applicant has been declared suitable;
  • The applicant’s stated order of preference;
  • Availability of the relevant position.

Successful candidates will receive an offer by email and must confirm acceptance within 48 hours.

Applicants who reject an offered position or fail to respond within the required period will lose the position and the right to receive another position under the same selection procedure. The opportunity will then be offered to the next eligible candidate.

Important Dates

The main dates published for the 2026 selection process are:

  • Application opening: July 2026;
  • Application deadline: August 26, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. CEST;
  • Publication of qualification-assessment results: by September 21, 2026;
  • Online interviews: beginning September 23, 2026;
  • Final ranking: by October 15, 2026 under the formal call;
  • Programme commencement: November 1, 2026;
  • Deadline for obtaining the B2 English certificate: October 31, 2027.

The programme’s application webpage separately lists October 10, 2026, as the date for final admission results, while the formal call states that the final ranking will be published by October 15, 2026. Applicants should therefore monitor the official IUSS call page for the legally effective result date.

Requirements for Successful International Candidates

Candidates who obtained their master’s degree outside Italy may be required at enrolment to provide:

  • A Declaration of Value;
  • Evidence that an application for the Declaration of Value has been submitted;
  • A Diploma Supplement, where accepted;
  • Additional documentation required by the university for recognition of the foreign qualification.

Successful non-EU candidates must apply for a study visa through the Universitaly platform within the period communicated after accepting the funded position.

After arriving in Italy, students must apply for a study residence permit through the appropriate Italian authorities within eight days.

The published call appears to contain an inconsistent year in the stated final-arrival deadline for non-EU candidates, because the date shown predates the programme’s November 2026 starting date. International candidates should confirm the correct arrival deadline directly with IUSS Pavia before making travel arrangements.

Registration Costs and Other Financial Conditions

The €30 application fee is non-refundable, including where an applicant is unsuccessful or does not complete the procedure correctly.

After enrolment, doctoral students are also required to pay the applicable annual regional study tax and stamp duty.

The funded position cannot normally be combined with another scholarship. An exception may apply to funding awarded specifically to support an authorized period of research abroad.

A person who has previously received an Italian doctoral scholarship, even partially, cannot receive another scholarship under this programme.

Full-Time Commitment

Admission requires full-time and exclusive participation in the PhD programme.

Regular outside employment is generally incompatible with the programme. Limited occasional activities may be permitted only under the conditions established by the university’s doctoral regulations.

Applicants who are currently employed should therefore review the applicable rules and assess whether they can commit full time before accepting an offer.

How to Prepare a Competitive Application

Because the research proposal and letter of purpose carry up to 40 of the 60 points available at the first stage, candidates should devote substantial attention to these documents.

A competitive application should:

  1. Select a research topic that genuinely matches the applicant’s academic training.
  2. Study the complete project description and the work of the proposed supervisor.
  3. Prepare a proposal specifically for the first-preference topic.
  4. Avoid submitting a generic climate-change proposal that does not respond to the advertised project.
  5. Formulate precise and feasible research questions.
  6. Explain the proposed methodology clearly.
  7. Connect expected results with practical sustainability or climate outcomes.
  8. Demonstrate familiarity with the relevant literature.
  9. Explain how previous education and experience support the proposed work.
  10. Follow every prescribed language and word limit.
  11. Ensure that transcripts and translations are complete.
  12. Submit the application sufficiently before the deadline to resolve any payment or technical problems.

Conclusion

The National PhD Programme in Sustainable Development and Climate Change 2026–2027 offers a significant opportunity for qualified graduates seeking advanced research training in climate science, sustainability, health, public policy, economics, engineering, technology, agriculture, energy and related disciplines.

With 35 funded positions, a three-year scholarship, an additional research budget, opportunities for international research and access to a nationwide network of Italian universities and research institutions, the programme provides both academic depth and practical exposure.

Applicants should not treat this as a general admission application. Every position is connected to a defined research topic, host institution and disciplinary profile. The strongest applicants will be those who select an appropriate project, prepare a focused research proposal, demonstrate a clear match between their previous experience and the proposed research, and comply precisely with all documentation requirements.

Applications must be submitted online by August 26, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. CEST. Candidates are strongly advised to begin preparing their research proposal, letter of purpose, transcripts and certified translations well before the deadline.

item.content:encoded:
Are you a young person passionate about online safety, digital well-being, gaming, and making the internet a better place for others? Roblox is inviting eligible teenagers to apply for its 2027 Teen Council for Civility and Well-Being.

The program gives young people the opportunity to share their perspectives directly with Roblox leaders and help shape initiatives related to safety, online civility, digital well-being, and the future of the platform.

About the Roblox Teen Council

Roblox launched its first Teen Council in 2024 to create a platform where young people could share their experiences and ideas about online communities. The initiative recognizes the importance of involving young users in discussions and decisions that directly affect their digital lives.

The 2027 Teen Council is expanding to include teenagers from Argentina, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru, and the United States. Through the council, selected participants will have the opportunity to provide feedback on Roblox products, safety features, and initiatives designed to promote healthier and more positive online experiences.

What Has the Teen Council Achieved?

Previous Teen Council members have played an important role in helping Roblox understand the experiences and perspectives of young users.

Members of the 2026 Teen Council provided feedback on features including Roblox Kids and Roblox Select accounts, as well as new chat tools. They also engaged with Roblox teams working in areas such as safety, marketing, and engineering.

The council also contributed to the development of a youth-friendly guide to Roblox’s Community Standards. The guide uses simple language to help younger users better understand the platform’s rules. Feedback from young people also helped inform improvements to Roblox’s in-game reporting experience.

In addition, council members worked with media literacy organizations on digital well-being initiatives, including a public service announcement and resources created for young people.

Who Can Apply?

To be eligible for the 2027 Teen Council, applicants must:

  • Be between 13 and 17 years old.
  • Live in Argentina, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru, or the United States.
  • Be proficient in English.
  • Have parental consent to apply.
  • Be interested in topics such as digital well-being, online safety, civility, and youth engagement.

What Is the Program Duration?

The next Teen Council is expected to run from October 2026 to June 2027.

Selected members will have the opportunity to engage with Roblox representatives, share their perspectives, and contribute ideas that could help shape the future of online safety and digital experiences for young people.

Why This Opportunity Matters

The Roblox Teen Council offers more than just a chance to participate in discussions. It gives young people a meaningful opportunity to have their voices heard by professionals working in technology, safety, engineering, marketing, and youth engagement.

For teenagers passionate about gaming, technology, online communities, leadership, or digital well-being, the program can be an excellent opportunity to develop communication skills, share ideas, and contribute to conversations about the future of the digital world.

Application Deadline

Applications are currently open and must be submitted by midnight PDT on August 18, 2026.

How to Apply

Eligible teenagers can apply through the official Roblox application form. Applicants should ensure that they meet all eligibility requirements and obtain the necessary parental consent before applying.

Application period: Open now
Deadline: August 18, 2026
Program period: October 2026 – June 2027
Age requirement: 13–17 years
Eligible countries: Argentina, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru, and the United States

Users aged 13 to 17 living in Argentina, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru, or the U.S. can now APPLY HERE for Roblox’s 2027 Teen Council.

Applicants for the Asia Pacific council can APPLY HERE

For more opportunities, visit OFY Website HERE

If you are a young person with ideas about how online communities can become safer, kinder, and more positive, this could be your opportunity to help shape the future of digital well-being.

Are you a university student passionate about communications, journalism, public relations, media relations, events, and the music industry? The Recording Academy, the organization behind the prestigious GRAMMY Awards, is inviting qualified students to apply for its Fall 2026 Communications Internship.

This opportunity is designed for students who want to gain practical experience in a fast-paced communications environment while learning how a major organization in the global music industry manages public relations, media engagement, events, content development, press coverage, research, and communications projects.

The internship offers the opportunity to work with the Communications Department of an organization that represents music professionals and operates some of the most recognized institutions and programs in the music industry.

The position is based in Santa Monica, California, with a remote option listed, and is offered on a part-time basis for the Fall 2026 semester.

Opportunity Overview

  • Opportunity: Intern, Communications
  • Organization: The Recording Academy
  • Industry: Music, Entertainment, Communications, Public Relations and Media
  • Location: Santa Monica, California, or Remote
  • Work Arrangement: Part-time
  • Hours: Approximately 20–24 hours per week
  • Internship Duration: One semester, approximately 12 weeks or equivalent
  • Program Dates: September 8, 2026 – December 11, 2026
  • Application Deadline: July 31, 2026
  • Compensation: The position pays applicable county or state minimum wage rates based on the intern’s work location
  • Academic Requirement: The intern must be able to provide a letter from their school confirming that they will receive college credit for the internship

About the Communications Internship

The Communications Intern will join the Recording Academy’s fast-paced Communications Department. The position is suitable for students who want to explore careers in public relations, media relations, strategic communications, entertainment communications and event communications.

The successful intern will support a variety of communications-related activities and gain exposure to the different stages of professional communications work.

The role requires someone who is highly organized, detail-oriented and comfortable managing multiple tasks at the same time. Since the position involves working in a dynamic environment, the intern should also be prepared to learn quickly, collaborate with colleagues and maintain a high level of professionalism.

This internship may be particularly valuable for students interested in learning how communications teams:

  • Develop media and press materials
  • Create content and identify story opportunities
  • Work with journalists and media organizations
  • Support major events
  • Track media coverage
  • Conduct research
  • Develop media lists
  • Prepare reports
  • Coordinate communications projects and administrative processes

Key Responsibilities of the Communications Intern

1. Draft Press and Communications Materials

The intern will assist with drafting press materials while ensuring that all communications follow the organization’s brand guidelines.

This may involve helping to prepare materials such as:

  • Press releases
  • Media advisories
  • Background information
  • Event communications
  • Internal communications materials
  • Other public relations content

The intern may also be expected to review and edit written materials when necessary. Strong attention to grammar, spelling, tone, clarity and accuracy will therefore be important.

This responsibility provides valuable experience for students who want to develop professional writing and editing skills.

2. Develop Story Angles and Content Ideas

The Communications Intern will be expected to help identify interesting story angles and fresh ideas for content.

This means the intern may need to:

  • Follow developments within the music industry
  • Identify topics that may interest media outlets
  • Suggest new approaches to communicating stories
  • Develop ideas for content and public relations campaigns
  • Think creatively about how stories can be presented to different audiences

This is an important responsibility for students interested in public relations and communications because effective communications professionals must be able to identify what makes a story interesting and relevant.

3. Support Media Outreach

The intern will help pitch genre-specific media and provide writers with the assets they need for their work.

This may include supporting communications activities involving:

  • Journalists
  • Music publications
  • Entertainment media
  • Industry publications
  • Online media platforms
  • Writers and content creators

The intern may also help gather and organize supporting materials such as images, background information, press materials and other assets needed for media coverage.

This experience can help students understand how professional media relations work is organized.

4. Participate in Events and Media Activities

One of the most exciting aspects of the internship is the opportunity to work at events.

The intern may support events such as:

  • Press conferences
  • Red carpet events
  • Media rooms
  • Other communications and entertainment industry events

Working at events can provide practical experience in professional event communications and media coordination.

Students may gain exposure to how communications teams prepare for and manage events involving journalists, industry professionals, public figures and other stakeholders.

This experience can be especially valuable for students interested in careers in:

  • Public relations
  • Event communications
  • Entertainment communications
  • Media relations
  • Event management
  • Corporate communications

5. Coordinate Event Production Paperwork and Project Trackers

The intern will assist with event production paperwork and project tracking.

This responsibility requires strong organizational and administrative skills.

The intern may help to:

  • Maintain project trackers
  • Update event-related documentation
  • Organize paperwork
  • Monitor deadlines
  • Track the progress of communications activities
  • Support the coordination of different project components

Students with experience using Microsoft Office applications and other productivity tools may find this aspect of the role particularly relevant.

6. Conduct Market Research

Research will also form part of the internship.

The intern may be required to conduct market research to support communications initiatives and help the department understand relevant trends, audiences, media outlets and industry developments.

Research activities may include:

  • Gathering information
  • Reviewing industry trends
  • Identifying relevant media outlets
  • Researching audiences
  • Supporting communications planning
  • Organizing findings for internal use

This responsibility can help students strengthen their analytical and research skills.

7. Generate Targeted Media Lists

The intern will help create media lists tailored to specific projects.

A media list may include relevant journalists, publications, media organizations and other contacts who may be interested in a particular story or campaign.

The intern may need to research and organize media contacts based on factors such as:

  • Publication type
  • Music genre
  • Audience
  • Geographic focus
  • Editorial interests
  • Relevance to a particular project

This is a valuable opportunity to learn how public relations professionals identify and organize media contacts.

8. Track Press Coverage and Prepare Media Reports

The Communications Intern will also help track press coverage and create media reports.

This may involve monitoring where and how the Recording Academy and its related initiatives are mentioned in the media.

The intern may help to:

  • Monitor media coverage
  • Record published articles and features
  • Organize coverage information
  • Track media mentions
  • Prepare reports
  • Summarize communications results

This can provide practical experience in measuring communications and public relations activities.

Who Is Eligible to Apply?

The internship is specifically designed for students who meet the following requirements.

Academic Status

Applicants must currently be enrolled in an undergraduate programme or graduate programme.

The role is particularly targeted at students pursuing studies in:

  • Communications
  • Journalism
  • Public Relations

Students in closely related academic programmes may also wish to review the official application requirements carefully to determine whether their academic background is suitable.

Academic Level

Applicants should be:

  • Junior undergraduate students
  • Senior undergraduate students
  • Graduate students

The internship is therefore not primarily aimed at first-year undergraduate students.

College Credit Requirement

One of the most important eligibility requirements is that the intern must be able to provide a letter from their school confirming that they will receive college credit for the internship.

This means applicants should confirm with their university or college before applying that the institution can provide the required documentation.

Applicants should not wait until the final stage of the recruitment process to investigate this requirement.

Key Skills and Qualities Required

The Recording Academy is seeking candidates who can demonstrate strong communication, organization and professional skills.

Strong Verbal and Written Communication

Because the role involves press materials, content development, media relations and communications activities, applicants should have strong written and verbal communication skills.

The ideal candidate should be able to:

  • Write clearly
  • Communicate professionally
  • Edit written materials
  • Present ideas effectively
  • Pay attention to tone and accuracy

Analytical Skills

The internship also requires analytical abilities.

This may be useful when:

  • Conducting market research
  • Identifying media opportunities
  • Developing story angles
  • Tracking press coverage
  • Preparing reports

Applicants should be comfortable gathering information, analyzing details and organizing findings.

Ability to Multitask

The Communications Department operates in a fast-paced environment.

The intern may be required to manage several responsibilities at the same time, particularly around events and communications projects.

Applicants should be able to:

  • Prioritize tasks
  • Meet deadlines
  • Manage competing responsibilities
  • Maintain attention to detail
  • Stay organized under pressure

Teamwork

The intern will work as part of a professional communications team.

The ability to collaborate with colleagues and contribute positively to team projects will therefore be important.

Applicants should be comfortable:

  • Working with others
  • Receiving feedback
  • Supporting team objectives
  • Communicating with colleagues
  • Contributing to shared projects

Microsoft Office and Computer Skills

Applicants should be proficient in multiple computer applications, including Microsoft Office programmes.

Useful skills may include experience with:

  • Microsoft Word
  • Microsoft Excel
  • Microsoft PowerPoint
  • Digital communication tools
  • Document management systems
  • Project trackers

Strong computer literacy can help an intern manage documents, research, reports and project information efficiently.

Professionalism and Confidentiality

The role requires honesty, trustworthiness and the ability to maintain confidential information.

This is particularly important because communications professionals may work with sensitive information involving:

  • Media relations
  • Upcoming announcements
  • Events
  • Internal projects
  • Industry professionals
  • Organizational activities

Applicants must understand the importance of professionalism and discretion in the workplace.

What Makes This Internship Valuable?

The Recording Academy is one of the most recognized organizations in the music industry. The internship therefore provides students with an opportunity to gain experience in a professional environment connected to the organization behind the GRAMMY Awards.

The experience may help interns develop practical skills in:

  • Public relations
  • Communications
  • Journalism
  • Media relations
  • Event coordination
  • Content development
  • Research
  • Project tracking
  • Media monitoring
  • Report preparation

The internship may also help students better understand the professional communications process from the development of a story idea through to media outreach and coverage tracking.

About the Recording Academy

The Recording Academy represents the voices of performers, songwriters, producers, engineers and other music professionals.

Its work extends beyond the GRAMMY Awards. The organization is involved in professional development, cultural enrichment, advocacy, education and human services initiatives for the music community.

The Academy also supports and works alongside important affiliated organizations and initiatives, including the GRAMMY Museum, MusiCares and the Latin Recording Academy.

The GRAMMY Museum

The GRAMMY Museum is dedicated to helping people understand the history and significance of music.

Established in 2008 through a partnership between the Recording Academy and AEG, the museum explores different aspects of music and the recording arts.

Its work includes:

  • Exhibitions
  • Education
  • Grants
  • Public programming
  • Music preservation initiatives

The museum explores subjects ranging from the technology behind the recording process to the artists and music professionals who have influenced culture.

MusiCares

MusiCares supports the health and well-being of people in the music community.

The organization provides confidential programmes and assistance relating to areas such as:

  • Financial challenges
  • Medical needs
  • Personal health issues
  • Emergency situations
  • Recovery and preventative support

MusiCares serves as an important support system for members of the music community who may require assistance.

The Latin Recording Academy

The Latin Recording Academy is an international membership organization representing Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking music professionals.

Its membership includes:

  • Recording artists
  • Musicians
  • Songwriters
  • Producers
  • Technical professionals
  • Other recording industry professionals

The organization produces the Latin GRAMMY Awards and supports educational and outreach initiatives for the Latin music community.

Internship Schedule and Working Hours

The Fall 2026 internship is scheduled to run from:

September 8, 2026, to December 11, 2026.

The internship lasts approximately one semester, or 12 weeks or an equivalent period.

The position is part-time, requiring approximately:

20–24 hours per week.

This structure may be suitable for students who need to balance an internship with their academic studies.

The position is listed as being available in Santa Monica, California, and remotely.

Applicants should carefully review the official application information to understand the exact eligibility requirements for the remote work arrangement.

Compensation

The internship pays applicable county or state minimum wage rates based on the intern’s work location.

Because the applicable minimum wage can depend on the location where the intern is working, applicants should review the official employment terms and confirm the compensation applicable to their location.

Important Application Deadline

The application deadline for students is:

July 31, 2026

Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day.

Those who need a college credit confirmation letter from their school should begin the process early, as obtaining official academic documentation may take time.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Students interested in applying should ensure that their application clearly demonstrates their suitability for communications work.

A strong application should highlight:

1. Relevant Academic Background

Clearly state your current degree programme, field of study and academic level.

Students studying communications, journalism, public relations or related disciplines should make this connection clear.

2. Writing and Editing Experience

Highlight experience involving:

  • Writing
  • Editing
  • Content creation
  • Press materials
  • Articles
  • Reports
  • Social media communications
  • Research writing

3. Media or Communications Experience

If you have experience with media relations, journalism, public relations, communications projects or event communications, ensure that it is clearly presented.

4. Event Experience

Experience supporting events, conferences, media activities or public programmes may be relevant to this internship.

5. Research and Analytical Skills

Highlight experience conducting research, preparing reports, gathering information or analyzing data.

6. Organizational Skills

Since the role involves project trackers, paperwork, deadlines and multiple tasks, applicants should demonstrate strong organization and attention to detail.

7. Computer Skills

Mention relevant proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and other tools used for document preparation, data organization and project tracking.

8. College Credit Confirmation

Applicants should be prepared to provide the required letter from their school confirming that they will receive college credit for the internship.

APPLY HERE

For more interneship opportunities, visit OFY Website HERE

Physical Requirements

The job posting states that certain roles may require employees or interns to:

  • Stand for extended periods
  • Walk for extended periods
  • Sit for extended periods
  • Work at a computer for extended periods
  • Lift or move up to 60 pounds

Reasonable accommodations may be available for qualified individuals with disabilities.

Applicants should review the specific physical requirements applicable to the role and work arrangement for which they are applying.

Equal Opportunity and Inclusion

The Recording Academy and its affiliates state that they are committed to equal employment opportunity and an inclusive workplace.

The organization states that it does not discriminate on the basis of protected characteristics, including race, color, religion, creed, sex, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, medical condition, military or veteran status, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information or other characteristics protected by law.

The organization also states that reasonable accommodations may be provided for qualified individuals with known disabilities unless doing so would create an undue hardship.

Final Thoughts

The Fall 2026 Communications Internship at the Recording Academy is a valuable opportunity for students seeking practical experience in communications, public relations, journalism, media relations and the entertainment industry.

Through the internship, successful candidates can gain exposure to press material development, content ideas, media outreach, event support, research, media list development, project tracking and press coverage reporting.

The opportunity is particularly suitable for junior and senior undergraduate students and graduate students studying Communications, Journalism, Public Relations or related fields. Applicants must also be able to obtain a school letter confirming that they will receive college credit for the internship.

With the application deadline set for July 31, 2026, eligible students should begin preparing their applications early and carefully review the academic credit requirement before applying.

This internship could provide an important opportunity to build practical communications experience while learning within the organization behind one of the world’s most recognized music awards.

Application deadline: July 31, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Artificial Intelligence is transforming industries worldwide, but one of the biggest barriers preventing widespread AI adoption across Africa is the high cost of cloud computing, expensive infrastructure, unstable internet connectivity, and unreliable electricity. To address these challenges, the Africa Deep Tech Foundation (ADTF) has officially launched the Africa Deep Tech Challenge (ADTC) 2026 – The Laptop LLM Challenge, a groundbreaking competition designed to encourage innovators to develop AI systems that run efficiently on affordable laptops already available across the continent.

Rather than rewarding teams for building the largest language models, ADTC 2026 focuses on creating practical, efficient, and locally deployable AI applications capable of running entirely offline. Participants are invited to demonstrate that cutting-edge AI can be accessible, affordable, and useful for millions of people without requiring expensive cloud services or powerful GPUs.

With a total prize pool of $20,000, mentorship opportunities, venture support, GPU credits, and recognition from Africa’s growing deep technology ecosystem, this challenge provides an excellent opportunity for AI developers, researchers, startups, and students to showcase innovative solutions that solve real-world African problems.

Application Deadline: August 25, 2026 (Gate 1 Submission)

What is the Africa Deep Tech Challenge 2026?

The Africa Deep Tech Challenge (ADTC) 2026 is an applied systems engineering competition organized by the Africa Deep Tech Foundation. Unlike traditional AI competitions that emphasize larger models or cloud-hosted systems, this challenge focuses on building practical AI applications capable of operating entirely on consumer-grade laptops commonly used throughout Africa.

The challenge encourages participants to optimize language models so they deliver strong performance while operating under strict hardware limitations. The objective is to democratize access to AI by ensuring advanced language models can function efficiently even where internet connectivity and computational resources are limited.

The competition emphasizes engineering excellence in areas such as:

  • Model quantization
  • Memory optimization
  • Efficient compilation
  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
  • Offline knowledge systems
  • Fast inference
  • Responsive user experience
  • Local data integration

The broader vision is to develop AI that people across Africa can own, run, and trust without depending on expensive cloud infrastructure.

Why This Challenge Matters

Across many African countries, accessing cloud-hosted Large Language Models (LLMs) remains expensive due to API costs, internet requirements, and inconsistent electricity.

The Africa Deep Tech Foundation believes the solution is not simply creating larger AI models but engineering smarter systems capable of operating on hardware that millions of Africans already own.

The competition highlights several important challenges:

Limited Access to Cloud AI

Many users cannot rely on continuous internet access or afford subscription-based AI services.

Examples include:

  • University students
  • Healthcare facilities
  • Small businesses
  • Farmers
  • Community organizations
  • Local entrepreneurs

Offline AI significantly reduces these barriers.

AI for Affordable Hardware

Instead of requiring expensive GPUs, the challenge targets affordable laptops costing between $150 and $500, making AI deployment far more accessible.

Efficient AI Engineering

Participants are expected to optimize every aspect of model performance, including:

  • RAM usage
  • Processing speed
  • User experience
  • Memory allocation
  • Model compression
  • Local retrieval systems

Competition Problem Domains

Participants must choose one primary application area while demonstrating at least one meaningful cross-disciplinary integration.

Available domains include:

1. Mathematics and Scientific Reasoning

Possible applications include:

  • Mathematical problem solving
  • Proof assistance
  • Scientific calculations
  • Quantitative reasoning

2. Healthcare and Medical Support

Potential solutions include:

  • Clinical question answering
  • Patient education
  • Healthcare information
  • Medical triage assistance

3. Agriculture

Innovators can develop AI tools that support:

  • Crop management
  • Livestock advisory
  • Weather information
  • Agricultural planning
  • Market intelligence

4. Creative Writing

Possible applications include:

  • Story generation
  • Editing assistance
  • Poetry
  • Multilingual writing
  • Content creation

5. Coding Assistants

Developers may create offline tools capable of:

  • Code generation
  • Debugging
  • Programming tutorials
  • Software development assistance

6. Enterprise Productivity

Business-focused applications may include:

  • Knowledge management
  • Internal documentation
  • SME productivity
  • Workflow support

7. Autonomous AI Agents

Participants can develop intelligent offline agents capable of:

  • Workflow automation
  • Privacy-focused task execution
  • Local orchestration
  • Offline decision support

REGISTER  HERE

Hardware Requirements

Every submission must successfully operate on the official ADTC Standard Laptop.

Target hardware specifications include:

Component Requirement
CPU Intel Core i5 (10th–12th Generation x86-64)
RAM 8 GB DDR4
Maximum Memory Usage 7 GB
Graphics Intel UHD or Iris Xe Integrated Graphics
Storage 256 GB SSD
Operating System Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
GPU No discrete GPU allowed

Any submission exceeding the 7 GB RAM limit during evaluation will be immediately disqualified.

African Language Bonus

Projects demonstrating meaningful support for at least one African language receive an additional 15% panel score bonus.

This encourages participants to develop AI systems that better reflect Africa’s linguistic diversity while improving accessibility for local communities.

Competition Timeline

The competition consists of three evaluation stages.

Gate 1 – Submission Package

Deadline: August 25, 2026

Participants must submit:

  • Open-source GitHub repository
  • Structured REPORT.md
  • Screenshots or demonstration clips
  • Two-minute demonstration video
  • Bonus documentation (African language support or budget laptop testing)

Gate 2 – Activities and Technical Audit

Dates: September 8 – September 29, 2026

Selected teams will participate in:

  • 30-minute technical Q&A
  • Reproducibility audit
  • Reviewer clarification
  • Optional benchmark updates
  • Optional feedback responses

Gate 3 – Final Package

Deadline: October 17, 2026

Finalists must prepare:

  • Maximum 10-slide pitch deck
  • Live presentation attendance
  • Technical setup verification

Scoring Criteria

Every submission undergoes standardized benchmarking using the official ADTC hardware profile.

Accuracy – 50%

Judges evaluate:

  • Automated benchmark performance
  • Prompt quality
  • Model correctness
  • Overall reasoning ability

Speed – 30%

Measured according to token generation speed relative to the fastest submission.

Efficiency – 20%

Rewards lower RAM usage during execution.

Lower memory consumption results in higher efficiency scores.

Additional Rules

Thermal Penalty

Teams lose 10 points if:

  • CPU temperature exceeds 85°C
  • Thermal throttling occurs

Automatic Disqualification

Submissions are immediately disqualified if:

  • The application crashes
  • Out-of-memory errors occur
  • RAM exceeds 7 GB

Performance Bonuses

Participants can further improve their scores through:

  • Budget Hardware Profile Bonus (+10%)
  • African Language Bonus (+15%)

Local Benchmarking Tool

To help participants prepare for official evaluation, ADTF provides an open-source local profiling tool that measures:

  • CPU utilization
  • Memory usage
  • Latency
  • Throughput
  • Overall hardware compatibility

This enables teams to optimize performance before submission.

Prize Pool

The competition offers a total prize pool of $20,000, along with additional technical and ecosystem support.

Grand Prize

The winning team receives:

  • $8,000 cash
  • Six-month scale-up residency
  • Venture Demo Day participation
  • Pilot matchmaking
  • ADTC Certified Trust-Mark
  • Governance and legal mentorship
  • Product hardening mentorship

Runner-Up

Prize includes:

  • $4,000 cash
  • Three-month residency
  • Pilot matchmaking
  • Venture Demo Day access

Best Integration Award

Awarded to the strongest cross-disciplinary solution.

Prize:

  • $3,000 cash

Best Localisation Award

Recognizes outstanding African language or local context integration.

Prize:

  • $1,500 cash

GPU Credits

Finalists

  • $250 GPU cloud credits
  • Up to ten finalists

Semi-finalists

  • $50 GPU cloud credits
  • Up to twenty semi-finalists

Ecosystem Partners

The competition is supported by a growing ecosystem of organizations dedicated to strengthening Africa’s deep technology landscape.

Partners include organizations across:

  • AI research
  • Venture development
  • Technology communities
  • Innovation hubs
  • Open-source communities
  • Developer networks

Frequently Asked Topics

Participants can expect guidance on topics such as:

  • Offline model evaluation
  • Hardware benchmarking
  • African language eligibility
  • Cross-disciplinary integration
  • Open-source model usage
  • Quantization tools
  • Deployment frameworks
  • Model size limitations
  • Accuracy benchmarks
  • Thermal monitoring
  • Hybrid versus offline architectures
  • Video demonstration requirements

How to Participate

Entering the challenge involves three simple steps:

Step 1

Register your project through the official submission platform.

Step 2

Work individually or build a team of up to three members.

Step 3

Read the competition rules, use the submission template, benchmark your model locally, and submit your complete Gate 1 package before the deadline.

Important Dates at a Glance

  • Gate 1 Submission Deadline: August 25, 2026
  • Technical Audit: September 8 – September 29, 2026
  • Final Package Deadline: October 17, 2026

To learn more about the opportunity Visit HERE.

Conclusion

The Africa Deep Tech Challenge 2026 represents an ambitious effort to redefine how artificial intelligence is developed and deployed across Africa. By focusing on lightweight, offline-capable AI systems that run on affordable consumer laptops, the competition seeks to remove barriers associated with cloud computing, internet dependence, and expensive hardware.

Beyond the attractive cash prizes, participants gain access to mentorship, technical validation, investor exposure, venture support, and recognition within Africa’s rapidly expanding deep technology ecosystem. Whether you are an AI researcher, software engineer, startup founder, student, or independent innovator, this challenge provides an opportunity to contribute practical AI solutions designed specifically for the realities of African communities.

If you are passionate about building accessible, efficient, and impactful artificial intelligence, now is the time to begin developing your solution. Be sure to prepare your open-source project, optimize it for the official hardware requirements, and submit your Gate 1 entry before August 25, 2026
